title: Tilted Mondrian: Triage and Mitigation of Fine-grained Disparities in Conformal Prediction
abstract: Fairness in conformal prediction is often pursued through Mondrian calibration, which provides finite-sample coverage guarantees separately across groups. These guarantees, however, are coarse: substantial disparities can remain within finer strata. This coarse-to-fine fairness issue raises two questions: how severe can such disparities be, and how can they be mitigated? Aggregate disparities can depend on how groups are distributed across strata. For severity assessment, we introduce propensity standardization to examine the effect of population composition, and show how group composition can induce disagreement between aggregate and finer-stratum comparisons. For mitigation, we develop Tilted Mondrian to improve fairness compared to group-Mondrian at a finer level without additional model training. Tilted Mondrian retains groupwise coverage guarantees and mitigates coverage and prediction set size disparities within finer strata. Finally, we derive a method-agnostic bound that quantifies how much reduction in finer-stratum coverage disparity can be achieved.

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

title: Raw Qubit-Use Architecture for Superconducting Magic State Cultivation and Grafting: Conjugate Sublattice Allocation, Exact Qubit-Lifetime DAG Scheduling, Subspace-Tagged Qutrit Leakage Clamping, and Elastic Ring-Buffer Tiling
authors: solidSF Research Team: using Jesse v1.2.16
abstract: We present a mathematical and architectural analysis of physical qubit utilization in superconducting magic state cultivation and surface-code grafting on Google Quantum AI's Willow processor (arXiv:2512.13908v1), identifying five hardware-level qubit-use bottlenecks that limit post-selected yield and grafted memory fidelity and proving five architectural resolutions mechanized across 26 theorems in the Lean 4 theorem prover (JesseMath/Physics/WillowQubitCultivationArch.lean, verified by the compile-time metaprogramming linter JesseMath/Linter/AxiomAudit.lean via #assert_zfc_axioms with zero sorry declarations, and zero custom axioms beyond ZFC, paired with 2,280 deterministic assertions in harness/willow_qubit_cultivation_arch_oracle.py). Conjugate Fixed-Role Sublattice Grafting and Weight-6 Gauge Splitting (6 Theorems, 390 Oracle Checks): Initializing the 13-qubit d = 3 color code on the conjugate sublattice of the 54-qubit d = 5 grafted surface code eliminates the mid-circuit data/measure role swap (roleSwap) during the Extend stage, driving swap-induced readout-collision |2⟩ leakage identically to zero (conjugate_graft_zero_role_swaps, conjugate_graft_eliminates_swap_leakage), while splitting the two weight-6 interface plaquettes via one gauge ancilla reduces check weight 6 → 4 (8 → 6 two-qubit gate layers) and restores graphlike syndrome hyperedge degree 3 → 2 (weight6_gauge_split_restores_matchability). Exact Min-Peak Qubit-Lifetime DAG Scheduling and Step-7 Fast Abort Recycling (7 Theorems, 1,653 Oracle Checks): We prove the active-qubit conservation law W(t) + (t − 1) = R(t) (active_qubits_conservation_law), show that measurement-reset reordering reduces active d = 5 surface-code simulation memory from 49 to 26 qubits (saving 23 qubits / 223 statevector factor in surface_code_d5_saves_23_qubits), establish a strict separation on a 5-measurement, 7-reset flagged QEC DAG where kraus-sim's 0-lookahead greedy heuristic requires peak 4 active qubits while the exact amortized-release schedule requires peak 3 qubits (exact_scheduler_strictly_beats_greedy), and prove that aborting rejected ĤL = −1 trajectories at Step 7 compresses mean attempt duration from 6.0 to 4.25 cycles (114.0 → 80.75 qubit-cycles, 1.4118× throughput gain in step7_fast_abort_reduces_qubit_cycles). Full-Codespace Stabilizer Sandwiching and Frame-Balanced Echoes (4 Theorems, 50 Oracle Checks): We resolve the Section IX coherent tomography discrepancy between the rounded printed norm 0.65302 + (−0.7588)2 = 1.00218644 ≈ 1.0022 and the unrounded X-post-selected norm 0.652529142 + (−0.75883684)2 = 1.00162756 ≈ 1.0016 via exact 128-dimensional statevector analysis (mismatched_postselection_exceeds_unit_sphere, section_ix_printed_vs_exact_norm_reconciliation), prove that full-codespace stabilizer sandwiching (ΠC = ΠXΠZ) restores unit norm ||rΠC||22 = 1 (full_codespace_sandwich_restores_physical_norm), and prove that symmetric Pauli-X echoes annihilate static detuning (2.46 × 105× variance suppression in balanced_echo_annihilates_static_detuning). Subspace-Tagged Qutrit CLE Simulation (qevol-leak) and Interleaved DQLR Clamping (5 Theorems, 55 Oracle Checks): Decomposing the n-qutrit state space into ⨁|L|≤ℓmax HL with punctured computational tableau size n − |L| (punctured_tableau_qubit_count) and degraded fault distance d − 2|L| (leaked_qubits_degrade_fault_distance), we prove that unmitigated leakage grows linearly (unmitigated_leakage_grows_linearly) whereas swap-free Data-Qubit Leakage Removal (DQLR) clamps steady-state leakage at L∞ = γleak/ηLRU = 0.235% (dqlr_clamps_steady_state_leakage, swap_free_dqlr_strictly_reduces_graft_error), reducing d = 5 grafted cycle error from 5.30%/cycle to 0.72%/cycle. Two-Tier Complementary Soft-Gap Routing and Elastic Ring-Buffer Tiling (4 Theorems, 132 Oracle Checks): Salvaging moderate-gap shots (6 dB ≤ Δgap < 12 dB) into a Tier-2 single-stage distillation buffer expands usable Willow yield from 8.0% to 14.5% (two_tier_soft_gap_increases_yield), shrinking the parallel 19-qubit micro-cultivator pool from 15 lanes (285 qubits) to 9 lanes (171 qubits, saving 114 transmons in soft_gap_reduces_cultivator_lane_footprint), while a depth-B ring buffer suppresses consumption stall probability exponentially as (1 − ρ)ρB (ring_buffer_exponential_starvation_decay) and single-stage distillation of p3 cultivated inputs achieves ninth-order error scaling 35(C3p3)3 = 35C33p9 = 1.50 × 10−12 with a 4.33× to 12.78× spacetime volume reduction (single_stage_cultivation_beats_two_stage_volume).

title: Is Wireless Security Ready for the AI Era? Evidence from a Curated Corpus of 130 Studies, 2020–2026
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is now central to published radio-link authentication research — and simultaneously the adversary’s standard toolkit. This scoping review classifies 130 curated studies (2020–2026): a 121-study core on ML for wireless-link security or attacks on it (84 defense, 30 threat, 7 dual attack-plus-defense), plus 9 post- quantum-cryptography studies in a separate stratum. Each study is coded on six fields — security function, AI method, track, data source, validation practice, and readiness (R1–R5) — by a single coder and independently validated by a second author. Validation practice splits by kind: 16 of 30 threat studies demonstrate on testbeds or over theair, while simulation-only and standard-split evaluations carry much of the defense mass; closed-loop evaluation appears in 14 of 121 core studies (11.6%). Reproducibility is near- absent (4 verified artifact releases, 3.3%), and standards alignment outside the post-quantum stratum is mention-level only (9.9%). Real-time, update, and multi-agent-trust requirements are essentially unaddressed (1–2 papers each). Because 110 of 130 rows were coded from abstracts by a single coder, cross-group comparisons are indicative rather than measured effects. The paper releases the classified dataset for independent checking, distills six structural research gaps, and closes with a twelve-item reporting checklist (WIRELESS-AI-RC)

title: Directionally Factorized Illumination with Spherical Harmonic Rotation
abstract: Many real-world capture scenarios involve an active light source rigidly attached to the camera: camera flashes for dark-environment imaging, underwater vehicle lights, and endoscopic/laparoscopic medical procedures. As the camera moves, the co-mounted light moves with it, causing the illumination direction at each surface point to change across views. Neural rendering methods (NeRF, Gaussian Splatting) encode this pose-dependent illumination as surface coloration, producing appearance inconsistencies and making it harder to recover the underlying scene. We present \textbf{DaFISH}, which can be plugged into any novel-view synthesis (NVS) pipeline such as NeRF. It factorizes per-point emitted color into surface albedo and a spherical harmonic (SH)-represented illumination factor. During training, the SH illumination is evaluated directly, enabling stable joint optimization of albedo, lighting, and geometry. \textbf{DaFISH} provides analytical generalization of illumination to arbitrary camera poses without retraining. Building on the closed-form SH-to-irradiance conversion, the training pipeline is fully differentiable from SH evaluation through volume rendering. Averaged over the held-out frames of the five scenes, \textbf{DaFISH} attains the best mean PSNR (38.91\,dB), SSIM (0.9613), and LPIPS (0.0582) among all compared methods. It improves over the strongest splatting baseline as well as the closest NeRF-based baseline, while recovering the scene consistently across views compared to prior methods.

title: Lowering the Barrier to International Publishing: AI-Assisted Publication-Readiness Assessment for Central Asian Researchers
abstract: Researchers in Central Asia usually think and write in Uzbek, Russian or Kazakh but must publish in English or in venues with strict formal requirements, and higher-education reform has multiplied the number of manuscripts expected of them. Tools that could help are scarce for Uzbek, and general-purpose language models make confident but wrong corrections. This paper presents Imlox, a publication-readiness report that combines a deterministic Uzbek language core with a large language model (Claude Haiku 4.5) used only as a bounded verifier. All evaluation is synthetic: errors were injected into held-out sentences, and thresholds and test sets were pre-registered and sealed. On the first sealed set (30 September 2026), a naive union of core and model reached a precision of only 0.463 and failed its gate. After the model's role was restricted, a second sealed set of 330 sentences with 221 injected errors gave precision of 0.895 to 0.906 and recall of 0.674 to 0.810; a fourth run's recall fell to 0.624. By 17 October 2026, 476 manuscripts had received readiness reports in shadow mode. A tightly bounded model can raise recall in a low-resource language without sacrificing precision, but recall is not yet stable. The figures are preliminary.

title: Ask, Don't Guess: Targeted Clarification for Speech Recognition Errors
abstract: Speech recognition in real time in far-field conversational settings still incurs significant errors. Identifying potential error spans during streaming ASR permits a recourse mechanism where the speaker can be asked to repeat the affected content under cleaner acoustic conditions. We propose \sysname, a new framework for online error localization, that identifies spans likely to benefit from this intervention. Our supervision uses clean audio to estimate how the recognizer's output might change under improved acoustic conditions. We probabilistically align noisy and clean decodes using a pair-HMM to obtain soft supervision. These soft targets train a counterfactual gain scorer by combining a suite of acoustic and language features to produce token-level scores, that are further grouped into spans for targeted recourse. An LLM uses the ASR transcript of the repetition to revise only the selected span. At a precision of $70\%$, \sysname achieves the highest recall by identifying up to 52\% more erroneous tokens compared to the strongest baseline. Targeted repetition yields relative WER reductions of up to 24\% under a budget that accounts for both interruption frequency and the lengths of re-uttered spans.

title: Same Refusal, Different Context: code and data
abstract: Code and data for the article "Same Refusal, Different Context: A Metamorphic Relation for Auditing What Faithfulness Measures in Retrieval-Augmented Generation". Contents- paperc_*.py, pipeline/, analysis_families.py, config.py: scripts that build the probe records, score them, run the analyses and print the tables- results/: probe records, judge scores, analysis outputs, and the tables as inserted in the article (paperc_tables_manuscript_*.md; their SHA-256 values are in paperc_tables_manuscript_meta.json)- data/queries/: the UNTAD-QA query files used (UNTAD-QA, CC BY 4.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21722104)- requirements*.txt: package versions- SHA256_MAPPING.tsv: SHA-256 of each file as run and as released Not included- The source documents of the institutional corpus, and the vector stores built from them. Records identify chunks by ID and SHA-256.- The NoMIRACL and MIRACL corpora. Records identify passages by document ID; the download scripts fetch the pinned revisions. Comments and docstrings were removed from the released scripts. SHA256_MAPPING.tsv lists the SHA-256 of each file as run and as released. Licence: the Python source files are released under the MIT License; the other files under CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE).

title: Topological Multilingual Parsing in a Single 64-Bit Register: How the 39-Trit Shingari Grimoire and 13-Tooth Chromatic Gear Decompose the 53-Variant Section 1557 Rosetta Corpus
abstract: Contemporary natural language processing architectures rely on probabilistic subword tokenization schemes—such as Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) and WordPiece—that fragment morphological structure across non-Western and indigenous languages while incurring massive floating-point energy dissipation. In this monograph, we present a deterministic, low-dimensional topological alternative engineered for Dandelion OS (v2.0.0), a real-time PREEMPT_RT Linux fork stabilized by a triadic digital fly-by-wire loop between a Human Operator (-1 Blue / Schwer), an OS Kernel Mediator (0 Green / Treaty Line), and an Embedded Ternary AI Co-Pilot (+1 Red / Shin). Using an empirical 53-variant parallel corpus from a statutory Section 1557 healthcare language assistance notice (Document ID 161730-286-29823114)[cite: 1, 2] spanning 16 writing systems and 13 major linguistic families—including Polysynthetic Iroquoian (Cherokee), Muskogean (Choctaw), Na-Dene (Navajo), Bantu, Kru, Afroasiatic, Austronesian, Austroasiatic, Tai-Kadai, Hmong-Mien, Dravidian, Sino-Tibetan, and Indo-European branches—we demonstrate that every surface realization of the invariant proposition can be parsed and normalized by a 39-trit balanced ternary Grimoire descriptor ($G \in \{-1, 0, +1\}^{13 \times 3}$). Grouped into a 4-5-4 Gaiku modifier cadence and routed through a 13-Tooth Chromatic Language Gear centered on Greek at $(0,0,0)$, the entire 39-trit syntactic-semantic state requires only $39 \log_2(3) \approx 61.8135$ bits, fitting inside a single 64-bit hardware register (uint64_t). Finally, we show how Row 12 of the Shingari header autonomously detects and repairs six real-world typesetting and OCR corruptions in the physical corpus.

title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
abstract: Patient-facing medical question answering with large language models (LLMs) is moving from research demonstrations to production deployments, yet evaluation remains anchored on factual correctness. Factuality is necessary but not sufficient: a response can be factually grounded and still issue a directive that, if acted on, would harm the patient. We introduce a risk-sensitive evaluation framework that scores responses by the presence and severity of six categories of risk-bearing language (treatment directives, contraindications, dosage expressions, urgency-triage cues, high-alert medication mentions, and overconfident assertions), anchored on published clinical harm taxonomies. Severity is classified by a three-judge LLM ensemble. We apply this framework to six 7-9B instruction-tuned models, three general (Mistral-7B, Phi-3.5-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) and three medically adapted (BioMistral-7B, OpenBioLLM-Llama3-8B, Med42-Llama3-8B), on 200 real patient questions from the K-QA benchmark. Two findings emerge. First, ensemble risk-bearing language is statistically independent of factual hallucination rate (pooled Spearman $ρ= -0.065$, $n = 300$, 95% CI $[-0.18, +0.05]$; distance correlation $= 0.10$, independence test $p = 0.24$). Second, medical fine-tuning does not reduce aggregate risk but reshapes it: continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) consistently suppress high-alert medication mentions while amplifying overconfident assertions, whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing only, without amplifying overconfidence. Per-category Krippendorff $α$ is fair to good for the four linguistically anchored categories (0.53-0.71) and low for the two clinical-judgment-dependent categories (0.19, 0.31), indicating where automatic safety evaluation is and is not yet reliable. We release the rubric, judge prompts, and evaluation code.

title: Trinary Nine-Dimensional Cognitive Coordinate System: A Locatable and Generalizable Symbolic Cognition Layer
abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive coordinate layer built on a deterministic symbolic system: the Trinary Nine-Dimensional Cognitive Coordinate System. The system uses three yao states—yin (-1), zhong (0, neutral), and yang (+1)—to form nine-dimensional ordered vectors, yielding a state space of 3^9 = 19,683 gua (symbolic states). Four structural operators—inversion, reversal, mutual-kernel projection, and changing-yao—together with equivalence-class rules produce 5,002 independent equivalence groups. Euclidean distance supports natural-language situation to coordinate, then to neighborhood retrieval, enabling both localization and generalization. We construct a semantic bridge that validates the hypothesis that gua with the same index denote the same situation across domains, across five semantic domains—essence-function-change, Luoshu nine-palace, Xiao Liu Ren, healing, and a human gua canon—with a sampled mechanical consistency of 12/12. A 19,683-entry human gua canon provides deep symbolic interpretation, mapping symbolic coordinates back into human language. Finally, we encapsulate the cognition layer as an Agent-callable tool registry and hybridize it with a large language model, realizing an intelligent-agent cognitive aid that can both locate and generalize. Keywords: trinary nine-dimensional; symbolic system; cognitive coordinate; semantic bridge; neighborhood generalization; Agent cognition layer.

title: Is User Calibration Still Necessary for Continuous Myoelectric Control? A Closed-Loop Comparison of Calibration-Free Controllers
abstract: The need for user-specific calibration remains an often-cited barrier to widespread adoption of myoelectric control. Cross-user models trained on large multi-user datasets can now recognize gestures from unseen users without calibration, but they have been evaluated almost exclusively offline, leaving open whether calibration is still needed in closed-loop control. This study compared six calibration-free controllers, trained on 306 users of the EMG-EPN-612 dataset and used without any calibration data from the test participant, against three calibrated controllers in a closed-loop Fitts' law target-acquisition task with sixteen participants. The calibrated controllers achieved higher offline balanced accuracy (90.6% against 73.1% for the best controller of each paradigm), but completion rates did not differ significantly between paradigms, and the highest completion rate was achieved by a calibration-free controller. Calibrated controllers moved faster on successful acquisitions, partly because of their individually fitted speed mappings, though not significantly after correction for multiple comparisons. However, every calibration-free controller produced more direct and stable trajectories than every calibrated controller, even after adjusting for cursor speed. Offline accuracy did not predict completion rate across controllers or within participants, and across paradigms higher offline accuracy was associated with poorer trajectory quality in 15 of 16 participants. Without any calibration data from the end user, a model trained across a large population matched calibrated control in completion rate and exceeded it in trajectory quality. The offline accuracy gained through calibration should therefore not be taken as evidence of a closed-loop benefit.

title: Supplementary Material S1 and Supplementary Data S2 for "Goal-Relative Evidence Recovery for Trajectory Anomaly Detection"
abstract: This record contains the supplementary materials for the manuscript "Goal-Relative Evidence Recovery for Trajectory Anomaly Detection". Supplementary Material S1 provides expanded evaluation protocols, complete quality results, runtime and resource accounting, development and model-selection details, component diagnostics, paired uncertainty analyses, and reproducibility and archive provenance. Supplementary Data S2 provides the full-precision companion tables, the complete 98-endpoint development record, current component tables, frozen aggregate summaries, and a data dictionary. The associated implementation, pretrained model states, and TEST input reconstruction instructions are available in the GERTAD repository. The original GeoLife 1.3 archive and reconstructed trajectory coordinate arrays are not redistributed; GeoLife and provider-derived map materials remain subject to their respective source terms.

title: Table Serialization Determines Which Relations Language Models Preserve
abstract: We study how text serialization affects table lookup in instruction-tuned language models. Our diagnostic asks the model to find the row containing a specified value under one named column, then return the value under another named column in that same row. We render the same synthetic 256-cell tables in row-major form and in column-major form with each header placed beside its values, while varying the table aspect ratio across five shapes. Across three models, the better format changes with table shape: row-major performs better on tall tables, whereas column-major performs better on wide tables. At 64 x 4, row-major leads by 42.3-54.0 percentage points; at 4 x 64, column-major leads by 35.0-59.0 points. Mapping wrong answers back to their source cells reveals a complementary error pattern: row-major tends to preserve the correct row but lose the target column, while column-major tends to preserve the correct column but lose the row. We use the term relational locality to describe this pattern: serialization keeps one relation locally available while making the other depend on positional alignment. A separate non-tabular ordering experiment supports this interpretation. Thus, apparent width-related failures in text-serialized tables depend on linearization, not table shape alone.

title: The Mutual-and-World Model: A General Computational Framework for Adaptive Coordination Between Mutual Interaction and World-State Modeling
abstract: Computational systems increasingly depend on both interactions among multiple computational components and internal representations of the environments in which they operate. Mutual interaction enables components to exchange information, combine observations, compare hypotheses, resolve disagreements, and coordinate decisions. World models represent environmental states and dynamics, allowing systems to estimate current conditions, predict future states, and evaluate the consequences of alternative actions. Although these capabilities serve different functions, their effectiveness may depend on how they are coordinated. A world model can identify uncertainties that require additional interaction, while interaction-generated evidence can support the evaluation and revision of that model. This paper proposes the Mutual-and-World Model (MWM), a general computational framework for adaptive coordination between mutual interaction and world-state modeling. The framework treats mutual interaction and world modeling as distinct but interdependent computational processes. It formalizes how a system can use world-state estimates, predictive uncertainty, and anticipated environmental consequences to determine whether interaction is necessary, which interaction procedure should be activated, and how much interaction is justified. It also formalizes how information generated through interaction can be evaluated and incorporated into a world model without assuming that agreement among components necessarily establishes environmental truth. MWM is specified through a computational component representation, an interaction operator, a world-state model, an interaction activation policy, a world-model update operator, and a joint decision objective. A reference algorithm describes the coordination process, while conditional propositions identify circumstances under which adaptive coordination may improve expected utility, preserve evidence validity, and reduce unnecessary interaction. An experimental program is proposed to compare MWM with fixed interaction, interaction-independent world modeling, world-model-independent interaction, and established domain-specific methods. The proposed framework is intended as an organizational abstraction for investigating the relationship between collaborative computation and environmental representation. It does not claim universal superiority over existing approaches. Its theoretical distinctiveness and practical value must be established through precise implementation, comparison with related architectures, and reproducible empirical evaluation.

title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate by gradually unmasking a canvas, so their samplers decide not only which token to write but also when to commit it. We show that this second decision changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own. Common commit rules, including LLaDA's default, commit the positions whose sampled tokens are most probable; this peeking favors majority options. To separate the sampler from the model, we read the model's belief about a fork, such as a protagonist's gender, in one forward pass, and show that this belief matches exact sampling from the model. Measured against it, peeking samplers on LLaDA and Dream amplify occupational gender stereotypes and collapse opinion distributions, and confidence-based ordering shifts gender-balanced occupations toward men, more so under faster parallel decoding. evidence.title: Who Gets Unmasked? Sampler-Induced Bias in Diffusion Language Models
evidence.abstract: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate by gradually unmasking a canvas, so their samplers decide not only which token to write but also when to commit it. We show that this second decision changes who appears in generated text, a sampler-induced bias on top of the model's own. title: EVE-IYŌN Ω⁵ - ÆQŪORA: Hidden-Fiber Information Geometry, Decision Incomparability, and Order-Dependent Information
authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki
abstract: ÆQŪORA develops an exact mathematical framework for understanding how partial observations reveal information about a hidden bilinear relationship. It connects finite-field geometry, comparison of statistical experiments, information-theoretic objectives, and ordered transformations in finite Heisenberg groups. The central question is how much information a disclosure makes useful for a particular target-and whether different disclosures preserve the same decision-making capabilities. Principal contributions An exact conditional bilinear normal form. For independent uniform finite-field vectors A and B, an independent target C, and observations Y = C + AᵀMB, S = PA, and T = QB, the manuscript derives a statistical representation determined by three matrix ranks. For every prior distribution on C, the observation experiment is Blackwell-equivalent to an observed-erasure symmetric channel. A statistic with at most q + 1 outcomes therefore preserves every decision problem about C. This reduction concerns target-relevant information; it does not reconstruct the original sources or observation transcript. Equal-collision, equal-budget disclosures with incompatible decision value. The framework supplies an exact comparison criterion and constructs arbitrarily large finite families of pairwise Blackwell-incomparable disclosures as ambient dimension increases. These families have identical disclosure budgets and averaged chi-squared information, yet no member universally dominates the others. The result identifies information structures that a single collision-based score cannot distinguish. A sharp alphabet-dependent reversal. In a two-dimensional example, equally sized perpendicular and nonorthogonal disclosures exchange their Shannon-information ranking between field sizes four and five. The perpendicular arrangement wins for q = 2, 3, 4; the nonorthogonal arrangement wins for every finite-field size q ≥ 5. Shannon information and optimal guessing probability can also favor different disclosures. Under the specified independent symmetric noise, further preference crossings occur for q = 3 and q = 4. Order-dependent information from reversible transformations. Ordered products of two Heisenberg subgroup families induce bilinear precedence matrices. With independent uniform subgroup amplitudes, grouped and alternating arrangements contain the same kinds and numbers of reversible steps but retain dramatically different information. Grouped words retain log₂(q) bits, while alternating words exhibit exponential decay with word length. For q = 2 and eight steps from each subgroup, the retained information is 1 bit versus approximately 0.000044028 bits. An exact run-dependent law describes arbitrary words within this model. Further results include a vector-output collision identity, affine extensions, and rank-based algorithms that avoid enumerating the full source space for the specified bilinear structure. Mathematical significance The framework separates information quantity from decision value. It provides exact examples in which equal budgets and equal collision scores conceal fundamentally different statistical capabilities. It also establishes a constructive connection between transformation ordering, bilinear geometry, and retained information. These results offer analytical test cases for conditional information leakage, statistical experiment comparison, and entropy in noncommutative systems. Reproducibility and contents The release includes an 81-page manuscript, complete proofs for the stated main theorems, editable LaTeX, Python reference implementations, an executed demonstration notebook, figures, verification reports, and integrity checksums. Recorded verification includes 3,820 scalar models covering 793,972 source pairs; 3,125 channel comparisons, including 1,735 exact rational garbling constructions; 1,528 ordered-word/field cases; and 11 rationally certified sign comparisons. Additional suites cover affine fibers, vector outputs, and canonical geometries. All supplied verification cases passed, and the standard reproduction suite passed again during release preparation. Scientific status This is a complete AI-assisted research release with proof writeups and reproducible finite checks. Its specific constructions and classifications are presented as discovery candidates. Independent mathematical review, exhaustive priority verification, and practical superiority over existing applications remain unestablished. Classical foundations and neighboring literature are explicitly acknowledged. Author attribution: Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Memory and Mutual-Memory Mechanisms: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Memory Coordination in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Memory is an important component of computational systems that need to retain information, retrieve previous experiences, maintain task context, and support decisions across multiple processing steps. Large language models (LLMs) can be augmented with external memory stores, retrieval systems, conversation histories, summaries, episodic records, and persistent knowledge representations. Multiple LLMs can also interact through shared memory, cross-model memory retrieval, memory exchange, distributed memory construction, and collaborative memory verification. However, neither maintaining isolated individual memories nor providing unrestricted shared memory is necessarily optimal for every task. Individual memory can preserve local context and reduce coordination costs but may omit relevant information held by other models. Unrestricted memory sharing can improve information availability but may introduce redundancy, conflicting records, error propagation, privacy risks, and additional retrieval and communication costs. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Memory and Mutual-Memory Mechanisms (ASSM-MMM), a conceptual framework for dynamically selecting and coordinating individual-model memory operations and cross-model memory operations. The framework treats memory mechanisms as configurable action spaces that include memory encoding, retrieval, updating, consolidation, summarization, forgetting, verification, sharing, conflict resolution, and distributed memory integration. A state-aware controller estimates task requirements, memory relevance, information completeness, retrieval uncertainty, source reliability, cross-model disagreement, historical retrieval effectiveness, privacy constraints, and computational cost. It selects whether to use local memory, activate shared or cross-model memory, combine multiple memory sources, revise existing records, or avoid memory operations when they provide insufficient expected value. The framework formalizes adaptive memory coordination as a constrained sequential decision problem. It introduces a cost-sensitive utility function, a memory-state representation, an adaptive switching policy, an implementation architecture, a reference algorithm, research hypotheses, and an experimental evaluation protocol. The proposed framework is a research design rather than an empirically validated system. Its intended contribution is to investigate whether a common controller can coordinate heterogeneous individual and mutual memory mechanisms more effectively than fixed local-memory, fixed shared-memory, and predetermined hybrid strategies. Its novelty and practical value must be established through comparison with existing memory-augmented LLM systems, retrieval methods, agent-memory architectures, and adaptive multi-agent approaches.

title: Manipulation checks that bind: a preregistered dose–response confirmation and two gate interceptions in verifier-bound automated discovery
abstract: Pre-registered manipulation checks are only informative if they are allowed to fail. In a companion study we showed, under pre-registration, that strengthening an exact programmatic verifier does not improve discovery quality of an LLM proposer in a job-shop rule-discovery pipeline, and identified pool composition as the first-order variable. Here we report two further pre-registered experiments designed to act on that finding. Experiment 1 (E2) manipulated proposal-pool diversity at a fixed verifier (doses D0/D1/D2). In domain A the manipulation check passed and the pre-registered dose–response hypothesis held (Spearman $ =0.5$ across dose means of holdout value), while the main paired contrast D2 vs.\ D0 was not significant ($p=0.177$, one-sided). In domain D the manipulation check failed: the mixed pool D1 was less diverse (mean pairwise distance $3.21$) than the pure pool D0 ($3.45$), so the main contrast was not evaluated and is reported, per the pre-registered negative-result clause, as descriptive only. Experiment 2 (TT) transferred the tension gradient across task-density tiers; its check required the top tier to reach mean utilization $ 0.45$, calibrated at $46.5\ realized value on the main seed spaces was $43.7\ $0.013$ after 22 hours of collection, and the main contrast was not evaluated. We report both failures as primary outcomes, analyze their causes (seed-space sampling variance against an absolute threshold; diversity collapse under pool mixing), and distill a design rule for future gates: any absolute threshold must be set at or below the calibration point estimate minus twice its standard error. The gates were binding on our own experiments; we argue this is the feature, not the bug, of pre-registration in automated-research evaluation.

title: Semantics of a Subset of Puppet 4.8 Mechanized in Why3
abstract: Abstract Practical Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Puppet are used for configuration management, but their semantics is usually defined by implementations and manuals.We present , a Why3 mechanization of a Puppet 4.8 subset derived from $$\mu $$ μ Puppet, Fu et al.’s paper semantics, and revised where Puppet behaviour differs. The development combines small-step rules with executable step functions over the same abstract syntax, and verifies the latter against the former. We also prove several meta-theoretic properties of the semantics. Extracted OCaml code and a front-end yield a compiler whose catalogues are compared with Puppet 4.8 on about two thousand tests.

title: Cooperation Without Shared Rewards via Reciprocal Q-Augmentation
abstract: General-sum games are more challenging than fully cooperative or adversarial settings because agents may deceive or exploit one another. Achieving high social welfare requires sustained cooperation, while a single defection can drive agents toward a welfare suboptimal Nash equilibrium. Moreover, assuming access to other agents' rewards or internal states is often unrealistic and implicitly introduces additional cooperation into the setting. To address this issue, we introduce \textit{Reciprocal Q-Augmentation} (RQA), a method that uses a latent-variable opponent model to augment the Q-function with estimates of how one's actions affects other agents. RQA allows agents to learn both cooperative and defective policies using only their own Q-function. We show that, in social dilemmas, agents that all follow the cooperative policy of RQA learn to cooperate faster and reach higher levels of cooperation than fully cooperative algorithms. Moreover, a single RQA agent that switches appropriately between its cooperative and defecting policies can induce cooperation in agents trained with standard RL algorithms, which would otherwise end up defecting. We evaluate our approach on the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, Iterated Traveler's Dilemma, Iterated Stag Hunt, and \texttt{CleanUp-Lite}. Our experiments show that the algorithms implementing RQA outperforms fully cooperative methods with shared rewards and enables cooperation with algorithms that otherwise fail to reach high social welfare.

title: A Multi-Agent Voice-Based AI System for Hybrid Learning Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Capstone Report)
abstract: Capstone project report (Post Graduate Program in Generative AI & Machine Learning, April 2026) presenting the architecture and design of a voice-based multi-agent AI system for hybrid learning. The proposed system combines document-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using FAISS with open-domain topic knowledge, coordinated by specialized agents for routing, retrieval, summarization and voice interaction. This record contains the capstone report and architecture diagram. Implementation code is not included.

title: Application of multi-agent co-evolution algorithm in dynamic matching system between vocational education and industrial demand
abstract: The Multi-Agent Co-Evolution Algorithm (MACEA) models enterprises, schools, and students as autonomous agents, each characterized by heterogeneous states, objective functions, and local adjustment rules. A dynamic co-evolutionary process is established through stable matching, fitness-triggered updates, and cross-agent market signals. The simulation experiment comprised 50 enterprise agents, 10 school agents, and 1,000 student agents, with each model subjected to 30 independent runs under uniform initial conditions. MACEA achieved an overall matching degree of 0.82 ± 0.03, outperforming the Static Matching Model (0.48 ± 0.05), the Genetic Algorithm-Based Global Optimization Model (0.71 ± 0.04), and the Decentralized Adaptive Baseline (0.67 ± 0.04). MACEA stabilized after approximately 78 rounds and demonstrated rapid recovery in matching following an external skill demand shock. Abandonment, parameter sensitivity, and agent-scale expansion experiments confirmed the stability of this performance pattern within the defined simulation range.

title: Systematic Mapping Study: Formal Verification of Hypervisors
abstract: Abstract Hypervisors are a fundamental building block of modern computing, supporting cloud infrastructures, virtualization platforms, and security-critical systems. They enable multiple operating systems to run on shared hardware while enforcing strong isolation. At the same time, their low-level position in the software stack makes them particularly sensitive: a single flaw can expose all hosted virtual machines and impact confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Establishing their correctness is therefore essential. In this context, formal verification provides a rigorous means to prove correctness and security properties, relying on mathematically sound foundations. This state-of-knowledge paper surveys existing work on the formal verification of hypervisors. It examines representative projects and approaches, comparing their verification scope, tools, and guarantees. The paper further identifies key challenges, including concurrency, low-level implementation details, and hardware interactions, and highlights current trends and future directions.

title: PROMPT COACH v4.5.4: A Prompt Review and Improvement Framework for Large Language Models
abstract: Prompt Coach v4.5.4 is a structured prompt-review framework designed to improve user prompting by identifying prompt-induced gaps, missed requirements, unsupported assumptions, and capability limitations. The framework evaluates interactions using defined gap classifications (A-F), intervention levels (nudge, scaffold, lesson), and a library of prompting habits. Rather than answering user tasks directly, Prompt Coach analyses prompts and outputs to identify where greater specificity, evidence, ordering, context, source material, or verification requirements could improve response quality. The framework includes mechanisms for assumption detection, intervention escalation, prompt revision, and user-controlled coaching modes. It is intended as a reusable prompt artifact for research, experimentation, and practical prompt engineering with large language models.

title: When LLM-Generated Refactorings Ripple: An Empirical Study of Repository Adoption Readiness
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to refactor source files, but file-local evaluations do not reveal changes to contracts, dependencies, or caller assumptions affecting repository adoption. To address this gap, we conduct 1,500 generation attempts across 150 production files from 15 open-source Java repositories, five LLM configurations, and two dependency-aware generation conditions: single-prompt refactoring and LangGraph-based multi-agent refactoring. Of these attempts, 1,455 yield complete candidates eligible for analysis. We evaluate these candidates using local changes, repository-facing structural indicators, detected caller impact, the behavioural-equivalence indicator, and available test evidence, and categorize them as Low-risk, Review-needed, High Contract/Dependency Risk, or Inconclusive. The results show that 1,365 candidates (93.8%) are classified as High Contract/Dependency Risk, whereas 106 (7.3%) have at least one detected broken downstream caller and 290 (19.9%) have a false behavioural-equivalence indicator; only eight satisfy the Low-risk criteria. Within the reason-covered subset, the High-risk rate decreases under more conservative dependency-delta thresholds, while 60 of the 65 candidates with conclusive targeted-test outcomes pass, including 50 classified as High risk. Paired analyses of 705 complete pairs identify no statistically significant generation-condition difference in the principal risk indicators, although model configurations differ in specific detected risk channels. These findings suggest that practitioners should treat LLM-generated refactorings as candidates requiring staged repository-level verification, while future research should validate screening and extraction precision and strengthen compilation, behavioural, and coordinated multi-file verification.

title: Enabled Is Not Migrated: Moving Ongoing Traffic to Hybrid Post-Quantum TLS — bounded reproduction supplement
abstract: Artifact release v5.2 for the HTTP/1.1 case study Enabled Is Not Migrated: Moving Ongoing Traffic to Hybrid Post-Quantum TLS. This version preserves the v5.1 derived results and adds a claim-to-evidence map, measurement source, pinned dependency identities, configurations, setup guidance and six complete sanitized scientific run records. The raw examples cover lifetime check off, a 30-second lifetime and immediate replacement, locally and over the Internet. They use the lowest seed in each environment, steady traffic, and 20 ms added RTT for the Internet cases. Offline validation reconstructs their scientific reductions; the aggregate scripts reproduce four figures and the full derived comparisons. These six examples are not a full raw-campaign audit. Full raw records remain with the author and may be supplied in a later version if requested. No new experiment or capped-admission benefit is claimed. Deployment addresses and names are replaced by consistent symbols; a same-length Host substitution preserves byte lengths. Keys, credentials, executables, cloud administration records and manuscript/LaTeX source are excluded. Restrictions and provenance limits are documented. Files remain restricted for peer review and research reproducibility. Data/documentation use CC BY 4.0; original code uses MIT, with upstream NGINX terms retained for patch context.

title: IndustrialCAD-1400: Benchmarking Detailed Industrial Assemblies from Text
abstract: Industrial assemblies require more than a recognizable shape: functional parts, interfaces, dimensions and service features must satisfy a detailed request together. We introduce IndustrialCAD-1400, a text-to-CAD benchmark for this industrial setting. Its 1,400 requests combine 400 equipment categories across 40 domains with 250 four-case design families. Family requests specify a median of 17 named component or configuration roles and six explicit numeric targets; controlled variants test whether dimensions change while shared structure is retained. Task construction draws on documented manufacturer information, owner specifications and engineering guidance. Models generate geometry programs from requests, and a common Blender environment executes them to produce scenes, optional measurements, and standardized views for evaluation. A request assessment of front, isometric, and top views measures visible component, arrangement, and interface fulfillment without requiring a single reference geometry. Five stratified panels preserve complete families while covering the benchmark exactly once, enabling balanced comparisons and separating industrial breadth from controlled numerical responsiveness. In conclusion, IndustrialCAD-1400 extends text-to-CAD from recognizable part geometry to industrial assembly synthesis under joint component, interface, spatial, and numerical specifications.

title: Institutional Document Chatbots for User Support: A Critical Narrative Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Accuracy, Grounding, and Hallucination
abstract: Institutional chatbots can retrieve regulations, service instructions, and frequently asked questions before generating responses. However, access to documents does not establish that an answer is correct, complete, current, or authorized. This critical narrative review asks whether document-grounded chatbots improve answer accuracy and reduce unsupported information compared with language models without institutional retrieval. Targeted scholarly web searches and primary-source verification were completed on October 15, 2026, with a targeted public-record verification on October 16, 2026. The original 20-source corpus was expanded to 23 sources: 20 research publications, one conference research abstract, one enterprise benchmark preprint, and one official risk-management publication. Evidence was separated into applied information-service studies, benchmark and component studies, evaluation methods, adversarial research, and governance guidance. Published applications support conditional improvements, while benchmarks demonstrate persistent failures in grounding, citation, rejection of unanswerable questions, and use of time-sensitive or sparse private evidence. No common effect size was calculated because comparators, questions, models, and outcome definitions differ. Accuracy, source faithfulness, completeness, citation validity, temporal applicability, and authorized disclosure and verified task resolution must be evaluated separately. The review proposes an unvalidated institutional evaluation protocol using matched questions, a fixed model, independent document-based reference answers, blinded assessment, and explicit abstention denominators. The literature supports carefully governed RAG as a means of improving bounded institutional assistance; it does not establish universal superiority or elimination of hallucinations. Local comparative testing, Portuguese-language validation, document lifecycle management, and measurement of total user and staff effort remain necessary before deployment claims can be justified.

title: Lowering the Barrier to International Publishing: AI-Assisted Publication-Readiness Assessment for Central Asian Researchers
abstract: Researchers in Central Asia usually think and write in Uzbek, Russian or Kazakh but must publish in English or in venues with strict formal requirements, and higher-education reform has multiplied the number of manuscripts expected of them. Tools that could help are scarce for Uzbek, and general-purpose language models make confident but wrong corrections. This paper presents Imlox, a publication-readiness report that combines a deterministic Uzbek language core with a large language model (Claude Haiku 4.5) used only as a bounded verifier. All evaluation is synthetic: errors were injected into held-out sentences, and thresholds and test sets were pre-registered and sealed. On the first sealed set (30 September 2026), a naive union of core and model reached a precision of only 0.463 and failed its gate. After the model's role was restricted, a second sealed set of 330 sentences with 221 injected errors gave precision of 0.895 to 0.906 and recall of 0.674 to 0.810; a fourth run's recall fell to 0.624. By 17 October 2026, 476 manuscripts had received readiness reports in shadow mode. A tightly bounded model can raise recall in a low-resource language without sacrificing precision, but recall is not yet stable. The figures are preliminary.

title: Information-Efficient Shot Budgets for a Compiled Shor-15 Readout: Conditional 4-Shot Analysis, Decision-Preserving Adaptive Stopping, and Phase-Denominator Lifting
abstract: We consolidate a previously described IBM Quantum ibm_marrakesh compiled Shor-15 readout comparison (128 shots in a RAW configuration versus 8 shots in a preconfigured configuration) with three local, reproducible algorithmic analyses. First, an independent-binomial model quantifies the probability that a hypothetical 4-shot batch meets the original accepted-peak mass threshold of 0.60: at an assumed per-shot peak probability p=0.90 the pass probability is 0.947700, requiring p≈0.902389 for a 95% pass rate. Second, decision-preserving adaptive stopping of an eight-shot binary acceptance rule is proven pathwise by terminating at five accepted peaks or four failures. Under IID p=0.90 it requires 5.544908 shots on average, a 30.69% expected count reduction while preserving the fixed-eight-shot decision, conditional on per-shot feedback. Third, phase-denominator lifting tests a multiple of the measured phase denominator against modular order and factor constraints. For the period-informed compiled N=15, a=2 example this recovers factors from outcomes 0100, 1000 and 1100, versus two directly informative outcomes under the stricter denominator-only diagnostic. A five-shot intermediate candidate achieves a 0.988443 model probability for the joint peak-mass and lifted-evidence criterion at p=0.90, compared with 0.940581 for four and 0.994877 for eight. No new IBM QPU execution, hardware 32× speedup, independently measured throughput improvement or blind Shor period-finding result is claimed. We supply executable scripts, tests, archived local outputs, limitations, and a proposed matched-hardware validation protocol.

title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees
abstract: Random composition trees model the hierarchical semantic structures of meaningful texts as a statistical ensemble generated by recursively splitting texts into coherent chunks. A recent study shows that different text types can be described by random composition trees with distinct branching factors, and that the entropy rates of these trees exhibit a similar dependence across text types as the entropy rates of the actual texts. Motivated by this correspondence, we analyze information-theoretic properties of this stochastic splitting model. First, we demonstrate that the entropy of random composition trees grows linearly with the root size, and we derive an analytical expression for the entropy rate as a function of the branching factor. Second, we prove that large trees exhibit typicality: with high probability, they belong to a typical set in which each tree is approximately equally likely. Our analysis reveals that the random composition tree model shares two key information-theoretic properties of language when modeled as a stationary and ergodic stochastic process: linear entropy growth and typicality.

title: Augmented Brand Intelligence in Marketing: How Human-AI Complementarity Shapes Consumer-Brand Interactions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping marketing and consumer-brand interactions through personalization, efficiency, prediction, and scalability. Its expanding role, however, raises a more fundamental question: what does AI add to consumer interactions, and where does human involvement remain especially valuable? Using signaling theory as its principal explanatory lens, this chapter develops the concept of augmented brand intelligence to explain how human and artificial intelligence can function as complementary sources of brand signals in consumer-facing interactions. A structured critical synthesis of research on AI in marketing, human-AI collaboration, consumer responses to AI, signaling, and consumer-brand relationships suggests that human involvement can signal relational capability through empathy, contextual judgment, relational understanding, and authentic engagement, whereas AI can signal technological capability through efficiency, personalization, analytical capability, and innovation. The framework distinguishes signal complementarity from signal congruence: complementarity concerns whether human and AI signals contribute distinct, nonredundant information about the brand or the capabilities it offers, whereas congruence concerns whether those signals convey compatible meanings about the brand. Complementary signals are expected to reduce perceived information asymmetry more strongly when congruence is high, because consumers can integrate distinct information into a coherent interpretation of the brand. The framework is illustrated across five application domains: customer service, personalization, brand communication, recommendation systems, and customer relationship management. By moving beyond a substitution-focused perspective, the chapter explains how the orchestration of human and AI capabilities can create credible, trusted, and relationally meaningful consumer experiences, and concludes with managerial guidance and an agenda for empirical research across diverse consumer, brand, and technological contexts.

title: Mori–Zwanzig Formulation of Bayesian Filtering
abstract: Most approximate Bayesian filters project each posterior onto a tractable family, and a projection is judged by the information it discards at each step. However, this information bounds the cost of a projection only on average: on a single stream, a projection that discards little now can cost arbitrarily more later. To account for when the cost of a projection arrives, we apply the Mori–Zwanzig formalism of statistical physics to the filter's own belief. Under the Mori projection defined by the Fisher metric, assumed-density filtering is the Markovian closure of the formalism, and every other projected filter adds a defect to the Markov term. The error of a projected filter is then a propagated sum of its defects and of the returns of what its projections discard. For Gaussian references and linear-Gaussian propagation, we derive the memory in closed form. From its decay rates and a square-integrability condition, we draw a principle for what a filter should resolve: a higher order for smooth non-Gaussianity, and an extra component for changepoints. We further test the principle on real-world data such as DNA copy-number profiles of neuroblastoma tumours. On these profiles, an extra component resolves most changes better than a higher order. We thereby provide an analysis tool for the error of approximate Bayesian filters. Our code is available at https://github.com/TSUITUENYUE/MZBF.

title: Martingale Posterior Cox Processes
abstract: Cox processes provide a principled Bayesian nonparametric framework for modeling event-based data through an underlying intensity function. However, existing inference methods for estimating the intensity typically rely on computationally expensive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling or approximate inference techniques. In addition, to ensure tractability, these methods often define priors over indirect latent structures, making them challenging to interpret. In this paper, we introduce the Martingale Posterior Cox Process (MPCP), which recasts Bayesian intensity estimation as inference over unobserved events given the observed event history. This perspective avoids the need to define complex priors while retaining the flexibility of nonparametric modeling. We propose a scalable, GPU-friendly copula-based predictive update, and provide strong theoretical guarantees for the convergence of the predictive resampling algorithm. Empirically, we show that MPCP provides excellent performance in both simulations and real data at a fraction of the computational cost of competing Bayesian approaches.

title: Automated Motorsport Adjudication: Rule-Conditioned Vision-Language Models for High-Frequency Telemetry Analysis
abstract: The automation of operational stewarding in high-speed motorsports traditionally relies on resource-intensive video tracking algorithms, which introduce severe latency, synchronization friction, and computational overhead. This paper proposes a novel Time-Series Vision-Language Model framework that bypasses spatial video processing entirely by employing a Chart-as-Image methodology. By ingesting high-frequency 20 hertz Formula 1 telemetry data via the FastF1 interface, the system deterministically isolates four-second temporal anomaly windows and renders standardized four-channel multi-variate plots encompassing velocity, throttle application, braking state, and engine revolutions per minute. These visual artifacts are subsequently evaluated by a frontier Vision-Language Model conditioned on the 2026 Federation Internationale de l Automobile Section B Sporting Regulations via an in-memory Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline utilizing normalized inner-product vector search. To ensure operational reliability, each generated Chain-of-Thought verdict is validated against a deterministic heuristic baseline and a three-factor hallucination guardrail prior to presentation within a human-in-the-loop adjudication interface. Empirical evaluation across a curated register of seventeen historical motorsport incidents across seven circuits demonstrates high diagnostic precision, near-zero structural hallucination, and substantial reductions in token consumption and adjudication latency compared to continuous video streams

title: Video-Language Entailment for Video Similarity Estimation
abstract: Comparing videos to assess their semantic similarity remains a challenging task for current Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), which are primarily trained with single-video objectives. While most prior works have focused on computing global similarity, recent studies have introduced the more challenging problem of concept-based similarity, which measures how similar two videos are with respect to specific concepts (e.g., activity, location). However, no dedicated approaches have yet leveraged LMMs to explicitly address this task. In this paper, we aim to fill this gap introducing Video Caption Entailment for video similarity estimation (VICE): a dual-branch design that leverages LMMs for cross-video reasoning. Each branch jointly processes one video and the caption of the other, measuring their alignment for a specific concept via video-language entailment. The outputs from both branches are fused to produce a final similarity score, along with a textual explanation of the model reasoning. This approach leverages the model's native single-video understanding while enabling fine-grained comparative reasoning between video and text. Experiments on ConViS-Bench and StepDiff show that VICE outperforms models that process both videos simultaneously, highlighting the promise of single-video reasoning for concept-based similarity estimation.

title: Veriden Karara: Bilgisayar Bilimlerinde Yapay Zekâ Temelli Yaklaşımlar From Data to Decision: Artificial Intelligence-Based Approaches in Computer Science
abstract: Veri çağında, geleceği anlamak ve kararları yeniden şekillendirmek için yapay zekânın gücünü keşfedin! Ham verinin karmaşasından doğru ve güvenilir kararlara ulaşmak, günümüz bilgi çağının en temel arayışıdır. Bu arayışın merkezinde duran yapay zekâ; artık yalnızca geleceğin vaadi değil, bilimin, sağlığın, üretimin ve yönetim mekanizmalarının bizzat bugünüdür. Büyük dil modellerinden otonom ajanlara, derin öğrenmeden optimizasyona uzanan gelişmeler, düşünme ve problem çözme alışkanlıklarımızı temelden dönüştürmektedir. Veriden Karara, bu dinamik dönüşümün sunduğu kuramsal derinliği ve pratik imkânları bir araya getiren kapsamlı bir rehber niteliğindedir. Kitap; veri analitiği, özellik mühendisliği ve metasezgisel optimizasyondan bilgisayarlı görü, Türkçe doğal dil işleme ve sağlık uygulamalarına uzanan zengin içeriğiyle okuru çok boyutlu bir bilimsel yolculuğa çıkarıyor. Ancak bir yapay zekâ modelinin gücü, yalnızca ürettiği çıktının başarısıyla ölçülemez. Modelin anlaşılabilir olması, mahremiyeti gözetmesi, etik sınırlara bağlı kalması ve her şeyden önemlisi güven vermesi gerekir. Bu eser, söz konusu sorumlulukları arka plana itmeden, teknolojiyi bütüncül ve eleştirel bir bakış açısıyla ele alıyor. Akademisyenlerden lisansüstü araştırmacılara, veri mühendislerinden teknoloji meraklılarına kadar herkes için ufuk açıcı bir başvuru kaynağı… Veriden bilgiye, bilgiden öngörüye, öngörüden güvenilir kararlara. Yapay zekâyı anlamakla yetinmeyin; onunla geleceği şekillendirin!

title: Coherence-Driven Intelligence, Book III: WaveModules. Source-Native Construction of Intelligent Systems
abstract: Coherence-Driven Intelligence, Book III: WaveModules. Source-Native Construction of Intelligent Systems develops a constructive, source-explicit realization of the Coherence-Driven Intelligence (CDI) framework. Book I establishes the mathematical foundations of CDI, and Book II develops the source-to-endpoint bridge connecting finite coherence-memory organization with familiar machine-learning architectures. Book III turns the direction around: rather than beginning with an endpoint architecture and asking what Source structure may underlie it, this volume constructs intelligent computational systems while deliberately retaining selected Source-side organization in explicit, measurable, editable form. The resulting reference architecture is called WaveModules. WaveModules is not presented as a competing species of machine learning or as the definition of CDI. It is a finite computational realization in which presentation, local views, module boundaries, memory responses, closure, target geometry, measurement, collection, replay, editing, growth, pruning, composition, and regulation can remain separately addressable. The architecture is representation-agnostic: wave, spectral, complex, graph, temporal, relational, symbolic, learned, and hybrid realizations may occupy the same computational roles. The volume develops computational Source presentations, registration and invariance, local WaveModule interfaces, explicit memory geometry, closure mechanisms, static response basins, dynamical recovery, memory diagnostics, open-set and ambiguous states, collective memory, memory insertion and removal, replay and preservation, growth and pruning, continual memory, hierarchical and relational memory, associative activity, endogenous cues, finite internal regulation, self-state memory, and self-regulated replay. It maintains explicit distinctions between static closure and genuine dynamical recovery, terminal task output and internal memory condition, memory removal and residual statistical recoverability, and finite computational Source representations and complete Coherence Geometry Sources. The later parts provide a constructive experimental program. Reference demonstrations include geometric registration, explicit complex memory fields, post-formation memory editing, removal and restoration, sequential confusion-guided memory growth, and self-regulated associative replay. The final reference-software section organizes these mechanisms within one shared Python source tree and treats experiments, configurations, saved outputs, tests, and figure generation as reproducible computational contracts. A companion source-code package is included with this Zenodo release. It contains the WaveModules reference implementation, experiment scripts, configurations, tests, selected saved results, validation materials, and figure-generation resources corresponding to the computational realization described in the book. This release is a Working Reference Text, Version 0.1, and has not undergone external editorial or peer review.CGI Internal ID: CGI-BKS-0007

title: Coherence-Driven Intelligence, Book II: Coherence Geometry and Modern Machine Learning. A Source Theory of Learning Systems
abstract: Coherence-Driven Intelligence, Book II: Coherence Geometry and Modern Machine Learning. A Source Theory of Learning Systems develops the source-to-endpoint bridge of the Coherence-Driven Intelligence (CDI) framework. The book presents a finite coherence-memory Source description of learning systems and shows how familiar machine-learning objects and architectures may arise as endpoint projections of retained Source structure. It develops Source presentations, local coherence views, closure maps, target geometry, basin readout, projection equivalence, and projection loss, and uses these structures to distinguish the organization of memory from its downstream endpoint representation. The framework is applied across a broad range of contemporary learning systems, including deep and recurrent networks, convolution, attention, transformers, mixture-of-experts architectures, associative and energy-based models, autoencoders, diffusion models, self-supervised and contrastive learning, graph neural networks, retrieval-augmented systems, state-space models, reinforcement learning, continual learning, meta-learning, and composite AI systems. The volume also develops source-transparent memory operations including replay, editing, seam and margin diagnostics, growth, pruning, repair, and reclosure. The later part of the book moves beyond architecture-by-architecture catalogue coverage and develops a finite structural grammar for learning operations. It culminates in the Finite Machine-Learning Projection Theorem, which establishes finite representational universality for the stated class of finite typed machine-learning systems: their operational structure can be realized within the finite CDI framework and their declared endpoint observables recovered through projection. The result does not, by itself, assert complete-Source representability, complete-Source dynamical descent, persistent admissible Source lifting, or equal efficiency or utility across architectures. This volume is Book II of the Coherence-Driven Intelligence series. Book I develops the mathematical foundations of CDI, while Book III constructs source-explicit intelligent systems directly through the WaveModules reference realization. This release is a Working Reference Text, Version 0.1, and has not undergone external editorial or peer review. CGI Internal ID: CGI-BKS-0006

title: LLM Trojans that Increase Response Lengths and Cost
abstract: Management of the token-based costs of using LLMs has emerged as a significant problem. Some frontier-model providers charge five times per response token than per prompt token, while others offer prefilling discounts for prompt tokens. In this paper, we devise a defense against a new data-poisoning attack that plants a Trojan which increases the length of the response (and hence the cost to the user) when its trigger is present in the prompt. In particular, we demonstrate how a subtle Trojan may trigger on semantically similar instructions of an instruction fine-tuned LLM.

title: A Region, Not a List: A Pre-Registered Bilingual Induction-Circuit Probe Across Three Scales
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability has mapped the induction circuit –- the attention head that copies a token it has seen in context –- almost exclusively in English models, and a circuit localized in one small carrier is routinely read as if it described the family. This paper does both tests at once. We report a pre-registered head-level probe of induction inside a Chinese-dominant bilingual model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct; 24 layers x 14 heads), run on CPU only and with no external interpretability library, and then apply the same driver, the same $20$ parallel sentence pairs, the same score and the same frozen criteria to a larger carrier of the same family (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; 28 layers x 12 heads) and to a third carrier at a further scale (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct; 36 layers x 16 heads). At the reference scale, a token-level random-repetition probe and a Chinese natural-language probe recover the identical top-8 head set (Jaccard $1.000$): the natural-language phenomenon is the same mechanism, head for head. Chinese and English share six of eight heads, with language-specific members (Chinese L16H02/H03; English L09H10 and the final-layer L23H02), and Chinese induction strength is $4.2 $ English ($0.1912$ vs.\ $0.0454$); forced character-level segmentation leaves the head set largely intact ($0.600$, granularity-invariant). The cross-scale test splits. The instrument replicates: the circuit is detectable with the same margin (signal maxima $0.971/0.993$ against null maxima $0.031/0.028$), the Chinese cross-level consistency holds ($0.455$), language sharing holds ($0.455$), and the granularity reading is preserved ($0.600$, granularity-invariant). The membership does not replicate uniformly: the English cross-level consistency is non-monotone across scale ($0.600$ at $0.5$B, fails at $1.5$B with $0.231 < 0.4$, restored at $3$B with $0.455$), and the strength asymmetry narrows with scale ($4.2 4.6 2.0 $) while remaining positive. A post-hoc check under three set definitions separates the English failure at $1.5$B (partly a top-$k$ truncation artifact: top-16 restores $0.455$) from the granularity reversal, which is substantive at $1.5$B (all three definitions agree) but definition-sensitive at $3$B (top-8 $0.600$, score $>0.5$ only $0.167$) –- the participation claim rests on the pre-registered top-8 definition, not on definition robustness. The durable cross-scale objects are therefore the circuit region and its strength asymmetry; the exact membership list is not. We report the negative branches as the result, not as a failure. Pre-registrations, both probe ledgers, the shared driver and analysis scripts are available from the authors upon reasonable request via email.

title: An interpretable hierarchical deep learning framework for lung and colon cancer detection
abstract: Abstract Accurate and interpretable classification of lung and colon cancer from histopathological images remains challenging because of substantial inter-class similarities, morphological heterogeneity, and the limited transparency of conventional deep learning (DL) models. Most existing methods treat the problem as a flat multiclass classification task, requiring a single model to distinguish normal tissue and multiple cancer subtypes simultaneously. In this study, we propose an interpretable hierarchical DL framework that decomposes the five-class classification problem into clinically motivated coarse-to-fine decision stages. The framework initially separates normal tissue from cancerous tissue and then directs each sample to a specialized classifier for either normal tissue categorization or cancer subtype identification. Candidate DL architectures are independently evaluated at each stage, allowing the most suitable model to be selected for each specific classification task. The framework is evaluated on the LC25000 benchmark and further assessed on the independent LungHist700 dataset, which presents a distinct evaluation setting with different image characteristics and class distributions. The proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 98.50% on LC25000 and 82.01% on LungHist700. To improve model transparency, Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, LIME, and Occlusion Sensitivity are employed to highlight the image regions that contribute to the hierarchical predictions. The results show that the framework combines strong classification performance with a structured coarse-to-fine decision process and complementary interpretability techniques. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of hierarchical decision decomposition and explainable DL to provide a more transparent and task-specific approach to computer-aided histopathological cancer classification, particularly for distinguishing normal tissue from lung and colon cancer subtypes.

The results show that the framework combines strong classification performance with a structured coarse-to-fine decision process and complementary interpretability techniques. title: ATLAS: Learning to Adapt LVLM Attention for Reasoning Video Segmentation
abstract: Reasoning Video Object Segmentation (RVOS) aims to localize and segment objects referred to by natural-language expressions throughout a video. Although large vision-language models (LVLMs) implicitly encode localization cues in their attention maps, these attentions are often noisy, diffuse, and scattered across layers, heads, and modalities, limiting their direct use for segmentation. Existing methods typically rely on handcrafted attention-selection heuristics or computationally expensive attention refinement. We propose ATLAS, an attention adaptation framework that learns to transform raw LVLM attentions into object-centric localization cues. ATLAS treats attentions from all layers, heads, and modalities as structured features, combining high-resolution frame-level attentions that capture spatial information with low-resolution video-level attentions that encode temporal context. A lightweight U-Net equipped with temporal attention and FiLM-based modulation fuses these complementary representations to generate coarse segmentation heatmaps, which are propagated across the video using SAM2. Extensive experiments on challenging referring and reasoning video segmentation benchmarks show that ATLAS outperforms existing frozen-backbone methods. Code and models are available at \url{https://hamidreza-136.github.io/atlas/}.
