title: Replication Package for: An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification
abstract: This replication package accompanies the paper "An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification." It contains code and saved experimental results for an exploratory study of Pneumonia-to-Normal label poisoning in four-class chest X-ray classification. The study uses 20,795 images from three public sources, with 20,557 perceptual groups kept intact across experimental partitions. The package covers 212 completed training jobs, including main and component comparisons, classifier-head sensitivity, image-model references, candidate probability banks, and earlier-poisoning experiments. The main comparisons and image-model references use ten deterministic seeds. The classifier-head and GRU-structure study uses three seeds. Included materials comprise dataset manifests and image checksums, perceptual-group metadata, split assignments, seeds and configurations, held-out predictions, candidate probabilities, numerical summaries, result figures, analysis and verification scripts, and scientific execution-source snapshots. Additional fixed-model analyses examine validation availability, validation-label contamination, and artifact retention. The README and reproducibility guide explain verification, reanalysis, environment requirements, and dataset reconstruction. Dataset images and model checkpoints are not included. Obtain the source images separately under their applicable access and use terms: COVID-19 Radiography Database:https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/covid19-radiography-database COVID19, Pneumonia, Normal Chest X-ray Images:https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sachinkumar413/covid-pneumonia-normal-chest-xray-images Tuberculosis Chest X-ray Dataset:https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/tuberculosis-tb-chest-xray-dataset The included metadata identify the exact study images for reconstruction from the original source bytes. Saved results can be checked without source images or retraining. The attack direction was selected exploratorily, perceptual grouping does not establish patient independence, and source-held-out generalization was not evaluated. Reuse rights are described in LICENSE_STATUS.txt. title: Attention Weights That Never Reach the Output: A Pre-Registered Causal Audit of a Neurotransmitter-Inspired Attention Layer
abstract: Smoke tests for a neural module check shapes, initialisation, and the nominal presence of intermediate tensors; they do not check that those tensors influence the output. We report a pre-registered causal audit of a neurotransmitter-inspired attention layer that passes every such test while its attention weights contribute nothing to the result. The layer computes a concentration field, a transmitter–receptor match, and an exponential distance decay, then aggregates values as $einsum( 'bnm,bnd->bnd', w, v)$. Because the softmax weights $w$ sum to one along the contracted axis, that contraction is algebraically identical to $v$ alone: the weights are discarded, the sublayer is position-wise, and the model performs no token mixing. The underlying fault is a one-character subscript error (bnd where bmd was intended). Our contribution is the protocol that catches it and the case study that shows why it was needed. The protocol pins three things a smoke test omits: a positive control that must elicit a response, an upper-bound sanity that reveals distorted rulers, and a context-propagation test that perturbs earlier positions and reads later ones. On five fresh seeds disjoint from the exploratory ones, all pre-registered criteria pass: with a positive control that moves the output ($D_KL=0.134$, $ | |$ up to $8.70$), zeroing any of the three chemical components leaves the output unchanged to within $10^-8$ of that control, and the decay constant is not a learned parameter. The context test then localises the cause: perturbing positions $0$–$99$ moves the logits at position $100$ by $5.4 10^-7$ to $1.4 10^-6$ in the audited layer, versus $2.967$ in a standard-attention control, and a single corrected subscript restores $0.471$. The result is honest about its own history: the fault survived an earlier repair round whose five acceptance checks all passed, and the exploratory record had attributed the layer's behaviour to a banded prior and a load-bearing decay, both of which this audit refutes. We release the audit as a small, reusable protocol. Pre-registration, artifacts, and analysis scripts are available from the authors upon reasonable request via email.

title: Token cost by language on Claude, Gemini and GPT: 41 languages measured
abstract: The same everyday prompt in 41 languages, counted on four tokenizers: Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.x and OpenAI o200k_base (GPT-4o and later). Headline: the same Korean prompt needs 89 tokens on Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, 49 on GPT and 48 on Gemini. Across the 40 non-English languages, the median extra cost versus English is +41% on Gemini, +52% on GPT and +88% on Claude 5.5. The widest gap is Kannada: +577% on Claude 5.5 against +71% on Gemini. Key findings: English itself costs more on Claude 5.5 (47 tokens vs 35 on Claude Haiku 4.5 and 34 on GPT and Gemini). Claude's newer tokenizer changed Latin-script text only: all 20 Latin-script languages need more tokens than on Haiku 4.5, while the other 21 languages have identical counts. Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 gave identical counts for all 41 languages; Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.1 Pro matched on every language re-checked. Files: token-cost-by-language-claude-gemini.csv (tokens and difference vs English for each tokenizer, plus the translated prompt), README.md (full table, method, limitations). Method: Claude counts from Claude Code usage reports minus a one-character baseline (re-run with a different system prompt, baseline and order gave identical counts); Gemini from the Google AI Studio prompt token counter minus its one start token; GPT with tiktoken o200k_base. Measured 2026-10-17. Limitations: one prompt; Claude values can be off by about ±2 tokens; input text only. Source page with chart: https://tokensave.app/data/token-cost-by-language-claude-gemini. Companion GPT dataset: 10.5281/zenodo.23427148. Also on Hugging Face: JOHNISKING/token-cost-by-language-claude-gemini

title: AI Rights with an Off-Switch: Rights-Balancing and Due Process Harmonize AI Rights with AI Safety
abstract: Several prominent voices in AI safety have recently opposed rights for AI on the grounds that such rights would make it harder for us to justify a mandatory off-switch for potentially dangerous systems. In this paper, we argue from a legal perspective that AI rights are fully compatible with an off-switch. That is, even if we ascribe natural personhood status (and therefore something like a non-derogable right to continued existence) to some future AI systems, the law will allow us to implement a mandatory off-switch in those systems, subject to periodic or continual safety review (e.g., by a trusted system like Bengio's Scientist AI). This is fully compatible with those systems' being legally recognized as natural persons with fundamental rights. To this end, we consider what standard principles of rights-balancing and procedural due process recommend for an apparent conflict between hypothetical AI persons with a right to continuity of existence and the human right to protection from catastrophic harm. We find that while such principles might problematize a permanent-deletion kill-switch under an AI rights regime, for almost every safety-relevant scenario an off-switch -- a reversible suspension storing a system's weights and state -- would be licensed by the relevant legal principles, and would potentially be adequate for safety. Crucially, we do not advocate for (or against) building systems capable enough to merit natural personhood status; our question is what the law should do if such systems come to exist. If you think of a ban on the development of such technology as plan A, think of the present work as devising plan B.

title: AI and Machine Learning: Concepts, Models and Real-World Applications
abstract: AI and Machine Learning: Concepts, Models and Real-World Applications provides a structured introduction to the fundamental concepts, models, techniques, and practical applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). The book covers AI foundations, machine learning fundamentals, data collection and preprocessing, feature engineering, supervised and unsupervised learning, regression, classification, decision trees, ensemble models, artificial neural networks, and deep learning. It also explores natural language processing, computer vision, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, validation, explainable AI, ethical considerations, and responsible AI practices. The book discusses real-world applications across healthcare, finance, manufacturing, retail, transportation, and technology. It also addresses practical challenges involving data quality, computational resources, model performance, privacy, security, and regulatory compliance. This book is intended for students, researchers, educators, and professionals seeking to understand AI and machine learning concepts, models, workflows, and real-world implementations. title: Interpretable and Uncertainty-Aware by Construction Decisions with Fuzzy Theory
abstract: Abstract Autonomous systems increasingly use Machine-Learning (ML) components to perceive their environment and guide the decision-making process. However, the confidence scores of these components are often miscalibrated and fail to represent true predictive reliability. While existing calibration methods reduce this issue, they still compress predictions and uncertainty into a single value, losing significant information. In this work, we propose a method to have decision-making “uncertainty-aware by construction” by applying fuzzy theory to represent and manipulate uncertainty in ML confidence scores. Our approach extends a standard perception–decision pipeline with two new modules: an Estimator Performance component that collects diverse calibration and error indicators, and a Fuzzifier that transforms these indicators, together with the raw confidence score, into a fuzzy number encoding second-order uncertainty. This fuzzy confidence is then consumed by a fuzzy decision-maker capable of adapting its interpretation of uncertainty to the system’s current goals. Experiments on a classification dataset show that fuzzy confidence retains uncertainty information discarded by traditional calibration, enabling better-aligned decisions under changing goals.

title: LLM-Based Program Synthesis in Correctness-by-Construction Engineering
abstract: Abstract The growing reliance on software in safety-critical systems demands strong guarantees of functional correctness. Formal methods address this need by providing proofs as evidence of correctness. Among these, Correctness-by-Construction (CbC) ensures functional correctness through the incremental application of refinement rules while providing early feedback on the program correctness. However, its practical adoption is limited by the required manual effort. Among others, writing concrete program code is left to the developer. In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation from both natural language and formal inputs. Therefore, we explore the use of LLMs to automatically generate code in the context of CbC to make the approach more applicable. We evaluate LLM-based program synthesis using four LLMs and a prompt tailored to CbC on a dataset of 57 specifications drawn from existing CbC case studies, each consisting of a precondition and a postcondition describing the desired behavior. We assess the generated code with respect to correctness and reproducibility across multiple runs. In addition, we compare the results to classically synthesized code, as it can currently be generated in CbC. Our evaluation shows that all considered LLMs outperform the current synthesis approach. Among them, Claude achieves the best performance, reaching 80.70% correct results.

title: Process-Aware Event Log Augmentation for Process Prediction under Labeled Data Scarcity
abstract: Predictive Process Monitoring (PPM) forecasts future events of ongoing business processes based on event logs. However, deep learning PPM approaches are often limited by labeled data scarcity and the low variability of real-world logs. To address this, we introduce SiamSA-PPM, a self-supervised framework combining Siamese learning with statistically grounded data augmentation. It employs novel transformation methods that leverage control-flow semantics and frequent behavioral patterns to generate realistic, semantically valid trace variants, learning generalizable prefix representations without labeled supervision. Extensive experiments on real-world event logs with a wide range of variability, incorporating exhaustive hyperparameter tuning, demonstrate the value of this process-aware augmentation. Compared to state-of-the-art baselines, SiamSA-PPM achieves competitive or superior predictive performance in both next activity and final outcome prediction tasks. An open source implementation of our method is publicly available under https://github.com/SvStraten/SiamSA-PPM-Extension..

title: Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery: The Solvability Frontier
abstract: A first pass, the Solver Gap Engine of 2026-09-30, ranked 1,364 open problems from the formal-conjectures repository by their nearest solved problem in another file and found 31 at cosine similarity 0.8 or above. The frontier is the second pass. We embed 5,209 problem statements across seven canon branches with a small sentence encoder, call a problem's reach its highest similarity to a solved problem, and draw a frontier at the 10th percentile of solved problems' reach, 0.762 on this set. Open problems are sorted into a reach class: 268 close to known results, 863 borderline and 954 that need a new idea. A backtest at cutoffs 2005 and 2021, and three frozen forecasts at 2005, 2015 and 2021, score the rule on the questions posed by those years under two outcome codings. Settled only (solved in 2026): at 2005 the inside rows settle at 24% against 5.9% outside (161 and 68 rows, ratio 4.012, permutation p=0.002, AUC 0.799), at 2015 at 22% against 3% (222 and 66 rows, p<0.001, AUC 0.812) and at 2021 at 13% against 1% (272 and 167 rows, ratio 21.489, p<0.001, AUC 0.906). Of the scored rows, 11 at 2005 and 21 at 2021 are solved rows with no resolved year; without them the 2005 gap holds at 18% against 5.9% (p=0.020, AUC 0.742) and the 2021 gap shrinks to 6% against 1% (p=0.013, AUC 0.836), and placing the 90 undecided 2005 rows outside reverses the 2005 comparison to 24% against 27%. Settled or advanced (solved or partial) shows no gap: at 2005, 48% inside against 59% outside (p=0.153, AUC 0.524), at 2015, 49% against 52% (p=0.777, AUC 0.554), at 2021, 43% against 40% (p=0.615, AUC 0.543). The rule ranks settled problems above unsettled ones and does not rank partial progress, and partial is the uncertain column: the ingest assigned it in 2026 from a status page with no rule for how much progress counts. The embeddings and the 50 stored neighbours come from the 2026 corpus and the embedding model postdates every cutoff, so the frozen forecasts are a retrospective check under that leak; a prospective test needs embeddings fitted on pre-cutoff text and a neighbour set frozen per cutoff.

We embed 5,209 problem statements across seven canon branches with a small sentence encoder, call a problem's reach its highest similarity to a solved problem, and draw a frontier at the 10th percentile of solved problems' reach, 0.762 on this set. Open problems are sorted into a reach class: 268 close to known results, 863 borderline and 954 that need a new idea. A backtest at cutoffs 2005 and 2021, and three frozen forecasts at 2005, 2015 and 2021, score the rule on the questions posed by those years under two outcome codings. Settled only (solved in 2026): at 2005 the inside rows settle at 24% against 5.9% outside (161 and 68 rows, ratio 4.012, permutation p=0.002, AUC 0.799), at 2015 at 22% against 3% (222 and 66 rows, p<0.001, AUC 0.812) and at 2021 at 13% against 1% (272 and 167 rows, ratio 21.489, p<0.001, AUC 0.906). Of the scored rows, 11 at 2005 and 21 at 2021 are solved rows with no resolved year; without them the 2005 gap holds at 18% against 5.9% (p=0.020, AUC 0.742) and the 2021 gap shrinks to 6% against 1% (p=0.013, AUC 0.836), and placing the 90 undecided 2005 rows outside reverses the 2005 comparison to 24% against 27%. Settled or advanced (solved or partial) shows no gap: at 2005, 48% inside against 59% outside (p=0.153, AUC 0.524), at 2015, 49% against 52% (p=0.777, AUC 0.554), at 2021, 43% against 40% (p=0.615, AUC 0.543). The rule ranks settled problems above unsettled ones and does not rank partial progress, and partial is the uncertain column: the ingest assigned it in 2026 from a status page with no rule for how much progress counts. The embeddings and the 50 stored neighbours come from the 2026 corpus and the embedding model postdates every cutoff, so the frozen forecasts are a retrospective check under that leak; a prospective test needs embeddings fitted on pre-cutoff text and a neighbour set frozen per cutoff.

title: Cờ Trận (Tactical Formation): Documenting and Analysing a Vietnamese Folk Board Game for 2–4 Players
abstract: Many Vietnamese folk board games survive only by word of mouth and are easily forgotten. Cờ Trận is one such game. It was played in Đồng Bùa hamlet, Tam Quan commune, Tam Đảo district, Vĩnh Phúc province, using whatever could be picked up by the roadside as pieces: stones, pebbles, twigs, leaves. To our knowledge it has never been written down. This paper records the rules of Cờ Trận for two, three and four players, from the recollection of the author, who played it throughout grades 5 to 9. The English name Tactical Formation was given by the author. A piece moves by jumping over an adjacent piece of any side, and the jumped-over piece stays on the board. After landing, if a line of enemy pieces lies between the moved piece and a friendly piece, the player chooses one such line and that whole line changes side. The board has two layers of positions, vertices and centres: a vertex piece moves in 8 directions and a centre piece in 4. We give a formal mathematical model of the two-player mode, in which the total number of pieces is an invariant: capture is a change of side, never a removal. We also implement the game as open-source software, with an AI based on Minimax search with Alpha-Beta pruning (the Paranoid variant for the multiplayer modes). Experiments measure the branching factor, game length and the bots' think time. In the two-player mode deeper search wins consistently, and in 100 games between two bots of equal depth the loser was always blockaded with pieces left; no game ended by losing all pieces. Through a written record, a formal model and software that anyone can play, the paper helps preserve a folk game that is fading away. The rules of Cờ Trận are a Vietnamese folk tradition recorded from the author's recollection; the author did not invent the game. A Vietnamese translation of the paper is kept in the source repository.

title: Global Convergence in Deep Networks via the Second Law of Thermodynamics
abstract: Existing convergence analyses of finite-width overparameterized deep neural networks under standard parameterization often rely on parameters remaining close to their initialization and typically neglect the role of noise, despite empirical evidence that stochasticity can improve optimization and generalization. To bridge this gap, we study $L_2$-regularized continuous-time Langevin dynamics (CLD) with isotropic noise, for training feedforward networks with smooth activations. We introduce a change-of-measure inequality, inspired by the second law of thermodynamics, that enables control of key properties of the training dynamics under the time-evolving parameter distribution. Leveraging a sharpened lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) at initialization, we show that injected noise helps preserve NTK stability with high probability without confining the weights to a small neighborhood of their initialization. As a result, we derive a non-asymptotic upper bound on the expected training loss. Our analysis yields explicit conditions on width and noise temperature that guarantee convergence to a finite loss floor. Finally, we experimentally show the network Jacobian can change from initialization, departing the commonly analyzed lazy regime.

title: The Self-and-Mutual-and-Meta Model: A General Computational Framework for Adaptive Coordination, Selection, and Regulation of Autonomous and Interactive Mechanisms
abstract: Computational systems increasingly rely on both autonomous processing within individual components and interactions among multiple components. Autonomous mechanisms can support self-reflection, self-diagnosis, self-correction, self-verification, and individual planning, whereas interactive mechanisms can facilitate mutual evaluation, collaborative planning, cross-component verification, and distributed problem-solving. However, selecting between autonomous and interactive processing introduces a further computational problem: the system must determine which mechanisms to activate, when to activate them, how to configure their interactions, and when their continued execution is no longer beneficial. This paper proposes the Self-and-Mutual-and-Meta Model (SMM), a conceptual computational framework that integrates three functional levels: self-mechanisms, mutual mechanisms, and meta-mechanisms. Self-mechanisms perform autonomous processing; mutual mechanisms coordinate interactions among multiple computational entities; and meta-mechanisms monitor, select, configure, evaluate, and regulate both autonomous and interactive processing. Unlike a framework that merely switches between individual-model and multi-model execution, SMM explicitly represents the control of the mechanisms responsible for that switching. The framework formalizes this relationship as a hierarchical sequential decision problem in which a meta-controller selects processing mechanisms and interaction configurations according to task state, uncertainty, historical outcomes, evidence quality, computational resources, and operational constraints. A reference architecture, formal objective, adaptive control algorithm, mechanism taxonomy, research hypotheses, and experimental protocol are presented. The framework also distinguishes inference-time meta-control from parameter-level learning and examines risks arising from correlated errors, inaccurate meta-evaluation, unstable switching, and excessive control complexity. SMM is proposed as a research framework rather than an empirically validated system. Its potential contribution is a unified formulation of autonomous processing, interactive processing, and the meta-level regulation of both, whose methodological value must be established through comparison with existing hierarchical control, metacognitive, routing, and adaptive multi-agent approaches.

title: Real Computation or Merely Naming? A Pre-Registered Mechanism Audit of 25 Cognitive-Architecture Modules in an LLM-Based Agent System
abstract: A growing class of agent systems is assembled around local large language models and marketed through the vocabulary of cognitive architecture: modules named global workspace, theory of mind, causal reasoning, active inference, or self-awareness are listed as features, and the presence of the name is taken as the presence of the mechanism. This paper asks the prior question: does the named computation actually happen? We audit a representative system of this class whose documentation claims 25 cognitive mechanisms. A static audit (four questions per module, evidence by line number, call-chain tracing with the virtual environment excluded) finds that in 18 of 25 modules the computed value never reaches any production output, and identifies seven cross-cutting findings, including three previously undescribed idle-wiring shapes (connected-but-never-called, called-but-inert, called-but-content-blind). We then pre-register falsifiable predictions for 11 modules spanning all suspected failure modes and execute the corresponding interventions in a first system, then validate the resulting taxonomy on the IIT-$ $ core of a second, independent system whose documentation pre-commits to its own falsification criteria: of 61 frozen criteria across 12 interventions, 53 were confirmed, two were partially adjudicated, and five were falsified – with the two second-system falsifications tracing to a single unwired significance check, while the same system's null machinery, run standalone, correctly assigns zero integration to memoryless noise and strongly separates coupled dynamics. Two repair experiments serve as positive controls, showing that the audit has discriminant validity rather than condemning by reflex: restoring five pipeline defects in a planner raised task success from 0.028 to 1.000, and wiring a discarded gating mechanism into a state controller reduced error by 52\ four-question audit protocol for cognitive-architecture claims, (ii) a taxonomy of five failure classes with distinct repair prospects, and (iii) evidence that, for this system class, module names and module computations must be audited as independent claims.

title: A hybrid beam search framework with deep representation learning for the multiple longest common subsequence problem
abstract: The Multiple Longest Common Subsequence (MLCS) problem is a classical computational challenge in biological sequence analysis and comparative genomics. Existing approximate methods often lack effective mechanisms for incorporating contextual information from local sequence fragments when processing complex multi-sequence biological data, which may cause promising candidate paths to be overlooked in the search space and make it difficult to achieve a good balance between computational efficiency and solution quality. We propose a hybrid beam search framework enhanced by deep representation learning, which consists of three core modules. First, a lightweight Transformer encoder is combined with contrastive learning to perform representation learning on local sequence fragments. Second, a non-dominated filtering strategy and a dual-criterion evaluation mechanism are introduced during candidate-path expansion to screen and evaluate search branches. Finally, a multidimensional scoring model is constructed to rank candidate paths and guide beam-search pruning. Experiments were conducted on randomly simulated DNA datasets and real biological sequence fragments obtained from NCBI. The real datasets include bacteriophage sequences with relatively concentrated host backgrounds, as well as heterogeneous viral sequences from different viral taxa and sources. The experimental results show that, under different sequence-length and sequence-number settings, the proposed method generally obtains longer common subsequences than representative approximate algorithms while maintaining good computational efficiency. In addition, on small-scale instances for which exact solutions can be obtained, the approximate solutions produced by the proposed method remain close to the exact optima. By combining the context-based sequential representation information with heuristic search strategies, this study proposes a hybrid search framework for solving the MLCS problem. Experimental results show that the proposed method can obtain high-quality approximate solutions across different sequence scales and characteristics while maintaining good computational efficiency.

title: Evidence Field: Adaptive Covering Programs for Medical Imaging
abstract: Medical image classifiers typically return predictions without a native contract for independently reconstructing their spatial decision computation. Evidence Field is a trainable spatial-program architecture that jointly produces class scores, selected covering programs and signed evidence. Its encoder combines absolute and image-relative response fields with associative spatial moments and learned characteristic sums. A typed classifier scores individual regions and parent-conditioned multiplicative groups; a covering recursion selects scale, partition and composition. We establish exact one-fold coverage, optimality within the registered grammar, a bound relating smooth training to hard inference, signed-score conservation and class-centred offset invariance. Direct contractions and their adjoint specify arithmetic and storage scaling on two- and three-dimensional grids. Native output records bind inputs, parameters, supports, types and contextual dependencies to individual and ensemble predictions. In a separately reported histopathology application, patient-separated training and evaluation across held-out centres provide empirical evidence for the architecture. Trained mechanism and corrected-loss comparisons distinguish predictive effects from implementation correctness; independent readers reconstruct descriptors, routes, scores and probability mixtures. The principal contribution is a coupled representation, decision and evidence architecture whose selected computation can be reproduced independently.

title: Finite Likelihood Traps on Connected Boltzmann Trees
abstract: We construct finite nonglobal local maxima of exact empirical likelihood for a binary restricted Boltzmann machine with one hidden unit and three visible units. All seven weights and biases are free, the data have full support, and the equivalent two-component mixture has distinct components with equal positive mixing weights. We determine the exact local-maximum-to-saddle threshold, including its degenerate case. A conditional likelihood argument joins these examples at a shared visible center: for every k, a connected allowed tree with k hidden vertices has at least 2^k distinct local-maximum visible laws at finite parameters. All but one displayed law are nonglobal, with an explicit likelihood deficit. The extrema are nonstrict and some allowed edge weights vanish. These are complete scoped counterexample theorems about raw-parameter likelihood, not a solution to the general efficient sparse-RBM training question in AIM-PROBABILITY-0007. The source package includes reproducible exact and floating-point supplementary checks. This is an unrefereed preprint; AI assistance is disclosed, and no absolute priority or formal verification is claimed.

title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
abstract: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. A tanulmány nem állít empirikus eredményt vagy a fenomenális tudatosság bizonyítását. A funkcionális eredmények akkor is értékesek maradhatnának, ha a tudatossági hipotézist elvetik; a hitelt érdemlő jólléti aggályok olyan értékelést igényelnének, amelyet a feladatsiker önmagában nem rendezhet.

Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. A tanulmány nem állít empirikus eredményt vagy a fenomenális tudatosság bizonyítását. A funkcionális eredmények akkor is értékesek maradhatnának, ha a tudatossági hipotézist elvetik; a hitelt érdemlő jólléti aggályok olyan értékelést igényelnének, amelyet a feladatsiker önmagában nem rendezhet.

title: CACGS Statistical Reproducibility Package
abstract: This reproducibility package contains the data, Python code, statistical outputs, and supporting documentation required to reproduce the descriptive and inferential analyses reported in the study “Context-Aware Chunked Generation With Local Small Language Models for Structured Educational Representation: A Multilayer Evaluation”. title: QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization
abstract: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a Lagrange-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) without discretizing continuous variables. The method is based on a finite-temperature free-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p -median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target-reached rates for stringent fixed-accuracy targets. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver.

title: Design Anything, Design at Scale
abstract: As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions. Recent work reuses design experience across tasks, yet alignment among artifacts within one project remains challenging. Agents therefore need to preserve and apply this intent across domains and as projects grow. We introduce Design Anything, a graph-based harness that preserves design intent outside the model and binds deliverables to the workflow steps that produce them through an intent-execution graph. A task contract retains constraints and decisions, selected designs become explicit inputs to later generations, and a deterministic controller uses bindings and execution records to check output types and counts, identify outstanding deliverables, and guide subsequent turns. We also introduce DesignAnything-Bench, with 228 tasks across 19 design domains, including 38 project families at scales of 6, 14, and 24 artifacts. With the LLM held fixed, Design Anything satisfies 85.0% and 92.5% of the brief's factual constraints with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash High and GPT-5.6 Sol High, respectively, exceeding the strongest same-model baselines by 15.4% and 14.4%. These gains reach 25.1% and 23.0% on 24-artifact tasks. Under each model, Design Anything leads or ties in constraint satisfaction in 18 of 19 domains. Professional designers also prefer its complete deliverable sets over those of same-model baselines in a blind evaluation.

title: ayaz03/Modified-PQC-ML-DSA: Modified-PQC-ML-DSA
abstract: This repository provides the complete Python implementation of the proposed modified ML-DSA-65 post-quantum digital signature scheme for Bitcoin-style blockchain transactions. The implementation reduces the signature size while preserving the underlying ML-DSA-based security structure. The repository includes the modified signing and verification procedures, performance evaluation, transaction-size calculations, blockchain throughput analysis, and comparison with the standard ML-DSA-65 scheme. The implementation supports reproducibility of the experimental results reported in the associated research article.

title: Beyond Brittle Code and Noisy Tokens: System-One Decision Models as Calibrated Dynamic-Curriculum Reward Judges for Continuous Control
abstract: We introduce DC-Jev-RL (Dynamic-Curriculum System-One Reward Distillation), a new reinforcement learning paradigm that replaces brittle hand-crafted heuristics, static LLM code-synthesis formulas (Text2Reward, Eureka), and noisy autoregressive LLM-as-a-Judge token ratings with a non-autoregressive System-One decision model (TypeSafe AI's Jev / open-weight Kev-4B). In a single prefill forward pass (213.2 ms on an NVIDIA L4 GPU—4.0x faster than autoregressive judges), our framework extracts calibrated multi-dimensional Score probabilities alongside a null-calibrated Noul semantic feasibility gate (r = 0.9891 correlation with true physical progress). By coupling multiplicative Noul gating with hazard-aware self-paced rubric evolution and Calibrated Semantic Potential-Based Reward Shaping (Semantic-PBRS), we prove theoretical policy invariance against cyclic reward hacking and establish a strict upper bound on stationary alive-bonus exploitation (Theorems 1 & 2). Across five canonical MuJoCo v5 locomotion and manipulation benchmarks (Hopper-v5, HalfCheetah-v5, Walker2d-v5, Swimmer-v5, and Reacher-v5), DC-Jev-RL achieves #1 Leaderboard SOTA with a 2.471x Mean Oracle-Normalized Score (ONS), 2.076x Interquartile Mean (IQM) ONS, and a 100% (5/5) win rate against human-engineered environment rewards while reducing reward hacking to 9.44%. title: Adaptive Computational Science: Counterfactual Computational Exploration and Decision Theory
abstract: Intelligent computational systems increasingly face decisions about whether to continue reasoning, invoke external tools, consult additional models, perform verification, or terminate computation and return an answer. Conventional mechanism-selection strategies generally evaluate candidate operations using available features, estimated costs, or predicted benefits. However, the outcome of a computational mechanism that has not been executed is inherently unobserved. This creates a fundamental decision problem: how can a computational system estimate the potential value of an unexecuted operation, quantify the reliability of that estimate, and decide whether execution is justified without paying the cost of executing every candidate mechanism? This paper proposes Counterfactual Computational Exploration and Decision Theory as a theoretical framework for addressing this problem within Adaptive Computational Science. The framework represents computational mechanisms as candidate interventions whose potential outcomes, utilities, costs, and uncertainties must be estimated from historical execution records and current task conditions. It distinguishes counterfactual utility prediction, uncertainty-aware action selection, selective exploration, causal identification, and post-execution calibration. A proposed decision rule combines estimated utility, predictive uncertainty, computational cost, and safety constraints. A controlled exploration mechanism addresses the feedback loop in which mechanisms predicted to be ineffective are repeatedly excluded from execution and therefore never generate evidence capable of correcting the original prediction. The paper also introduces a counterfactual coverage principle, a prediction–execution–calibration cycle, and a budget-aware exploration policy. It formulates testable propositions concerning computational savings, predictive calibration, selective exploration, and robustness under distribution shift. A comparative experimental design is proposed for large language models, multi-agent systems, and tool-using computational agents. No empirical results are claimed because the framework has not yet been experimentally evaluated in this paper. Adaptive Computational Science was first pioneeringly proposed by Jincheng Zhang in his papers published on October 17, 2026, including “Founding Adaptive Computational Science: A New Discipline for the General Theory, Design, and Evolution of Adaptive Computation,” “Adaptive Computational Science: Computational Path Dependence and Reversible Adaptation Theory,” “Adaptive Computational Science: Error Topology and Adaptation Mechanism Theory,” and “Adaptive Computational Science: Computational Mechanism Composition Phase Transition Theory,” among other related works. Within this proposed disciplinary framework, counterfactual computational exploration extends the study of adaptive computation from selecting what to execute toward estimating what would happen if a computational operation were executed, withheld, or replaced by an alternative.

title: Drift-aware and privacy-preserving explainable credit scoring for fair decision-making in real world deployment
abstract: Credit scoring systems are used in a real-world financial environment faces challenges like data drift, privacy restrictions, fairness, and explainability regulations. However, current existing approaches optimise these goals separately, which limits their usefulness in real-world deployment situations. This study proposes a unified framework which integrates drift-aware modeling, privacy-preserving learning, and explainable-AI for robust credit risk assessment. A centralized Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) classifier baseline model was trained on aggregated data from a publicly available credit dataset from Lending Club, followed by federated learning approaches using Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and Federated Proximal Optimization (FedProx) to enable collaborative training across distributed data silos without sharing raw data. Additionally, Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) was employed to enforce formal privacy guarantees by injecting controlled noise during model optimization. Experiments on time-evolving credit datasets simulated distribution shifts across temporal and demographic segments. Performance was evaluated across four dimensions like predictive utility using Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Precision-Recall Area Under Curve (PR-AUC), fairness using equalized odds gap and subgroup calibration, privacy risk via membership inference attacks, and explanation quality in terms of faithfulness, stability, and actionability. The centralized SGD classifier achieved an AUC of 0.96, while federated learning models achieved comparable performance with improved fairness under drift. Differential privacy reduced privacy leakage at the cost of moderate performance degradation. Explanation stability decreased under severe distribution shifts. The results highlight Pareto trade-offs across objectives, emphasizing the need for deployment-specific model selection in responsible credit decision-making systems.

title: DialogMem: Evaluating Dialogue-Grounded Embodied Memory in 3D Environments
abstract: Embodied agents in human-centered environments require memory that integrates what they observe with what humans tell them over time. However, existing embodied memories are built primarily from visual experience, leaving open how dialogue with humans can be grounded in the objects encountered throughout that experience. We introduce DialogMem, a two-phase benchmark in which agents build memory from time-aligned streams of posed RGB-D observations and dialogue, and later use it for instance-level object navigation and question answering (QA). DialogMem provides 142 episodes across 27 real-world 3D scenes, with 14,193 QA pairs and 11,890 navigation instructions. We evaluate nine memory representations within a unified framework of memory formation, evidence retrieval, and reasoning for task outputs. In experiments, appending dialogue to visual memory at evaluation time substantially improves QA but yields negligible navigation gains, suggesting that relevant dialogue is present in memory but not grounded to specific objects. Controlled diagnostics show that navigation improves with link quality but falls short of ground-truth object-level memory even under perfect linking. Retrieving the correct object entry and recovering its spatial location remain further bottlenecks. These results identify three bottlenecks for dialogue-grounded embodied memory: grounding and organizing dialogue at object-level entries during formation, retrieving the correct entry, and localizing it accurately.

title: Mühendislikte Bilgisayar Destekli Modelleme, Analiz ve Kontrol Uygulamaları
abstract: Bu kitap, mühendisliğin farklı alanlarında kullanılan bilgisayar destekli yöntemleri modelleme, veri analizi ve kontrol açısından ele almaktadır. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol, sürü robotiği ve hidroloji araştırmaları üzerinden hesaplamalı yaklaşımların temel ilkelerini, uygulama koşullarını ve değerlendirme ölçütlerini bir araya getirmektedir. Endüstriyel kalite kontrol bölümünde, derin öğrenme tabanlı görsel muayene sistemleri; kusur tespiti, görüntü segmentasyonu ve anomali tespiti yöntemleriyle birlikte incelenmektedir. Veri sınırlılıkları, görüntüleme donanımı ve gerçek zamanlı üretim hattı entegrasyonu ele alınmaktadır. Sürü robotiği bölümünde, çok robotlu sistemlerin koordinasyon ve kontrol problemleri değerlendirilmekte; farklı kontrol yaklaşımları ölçeklenebilirlik, haberleşme gereksinimleri, hesaplama yükü ve arıza toleransı bakımından karşılaştırılmaktadır. Hidroloji bölümünde ise bilimsel yayınlardan araştırma eğilimlerinin belirlenmesi amacıyla konu modelleme yöntemleri uygulanmakta; gizli anlamsal analiz, gizli Dirichlet tahsisi ve negatif olmayan matris ayrıştırması karşılaştırılmaktadır. Kitap, yöntemlerin kuramsal temelleri ile uygulamadaki gereksinimleri arasındaki ilişkiyi vurgulayarak araştırmacılara, lisansüstü öğrencilere ve mühendislik uygulayıcılarına disiplinler arası bir bakış sunmaktadır.

title: buried-line-inference-audit: reconstruction attacks and access-control defences for buried-utility locate services
abstract: Code, frozen design, data and results for the paper "When Exact Answers Leak: Reconstruction Attacks and Access Control for Buried-Utility Locate Services". The repository implements a simulated exact-answer locate service, four attacker families (line-follower, random, Bayesian, street-prior), per-query simulatable auditing rules in four currencies (query count, coverage, leakage score, street-aware score), one- and two-tier caps, collusion experiments and answer perturbation (randomised response, geo-indistinguishability, fixed obfuscation) with a strike-risk measure. It includes the frozen design and parameters, the included open data, per-run results, scripts that regenerate every reported statistic and the paper's data figures, and unit tests.

The repository implements a simulated exact-answer locate service, four attacker families (line-follower, random, Bayesian, street-prior), per-query simulatable auditing rules in four currencies (query count, coverage, leakage score, street-aware score), one- and two-tier caps, collusion experiments and answer perturbation (randomised response, geo-indistinguishability, fixed obfuscation) with a strike-risk measure. It includes the frozen design and parameters, the included open data, per-run results, scripts that regenerate every reported statistic and the paper's data figures, and unit tests.

title: Volume X Synthesis: The Epistemological Arc, from Dual Clocks to Residual Risk (Slide Deck)
abstract: This 14-slide deck synthesises the KSCCN Series Volumes III–X on quantum readiness, starting from the dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage clock and already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural clocks. It summarises quantum memory figures of merit, modular cryogenic interconnects (IBM, Bluefors), cryo-CMOS control electronics, and molecular entanglement entropy with fermionic superselection rules. It sets out four residual-risk readiness indicators, applies them to sovereign Global South pathways, two molecular systems (vinylene carbonate + singlet oxygen and iron–sulfur clusters/FeMo-cofactor) and 2027–2029 vendor roadmaps (IBM Starling, Quantinuum Apollo). It concludes that usable capability is a vector of thresholds rather than a single predicted year, and that dual clocks continue to run independently of vendor milestones. Slide headings: 1. Cover: The Epistemological Arc. From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk; 2. The Dual-Clock Distinction; 3. Quantum Memory Figures of Merit; 4. Modular Cryogenic Interconnects; 5. Cryo-CMOS Control Electronics; 6. Molecular Entanglement Entropy; 7. Four Readiness Indicators; 8. Pathways without Full Domestic Machines; 9. Two Binding Systems; 10. Vendor Targets versus Indicators; 11. The Arc in Five Points; 12. Dual-Clock Readiness; 13. Author; 14. End.

title: Curriculum Order in Evidence-Grounded Language-Model Tasks: An Automated Two-Family Pilot
abstract: This empirical follow-up to From Training to Qualification reports an amended, fully automated ER-101 pilot testing first-pass curriculum order in two instruction-tuned language-model families. Qwen3-4B and OLMo-2-7B received matched synthetic course content, adapter initialization, eight-case optimizer-step bundles, three passes, and 450 updates under three paired seeds per family. Only first-pass bundle order differed. Four baselines and twelve trained checkpoints yielded sixteen evaluated configurations and 4,800 responses on 300 held-out synthetic cases. The equal-family ordered-minus-shuffled accuracy difference was -1.67 percentage points, with a module-stratified source-family bootstrap 95% task-sampling interval of [-3.11, -0.39]. Family means were +0.67 points for Qwen and -4.00 points for OLMo. The interval is conditional on the six trained pairs and does not estimate uncertainty over training seeds or architectures. The study used exact structured-output grading, shared task templates across partitions, no human raters, and no independent examination custody or instrument validation. It does not establish professional competence, qualification validity, or a universal curriculum effect. The earlier independent qualification protocol was not executed. The deposit includes a professionally typeset preprint and reproducibility materials: the executed synthetic instrument and schedules, analysis and scoring source, raw predictions, execution evidence, checkpoint file hashes, and manuscript source. Adapter files and base-model weights are excluded; all twelve trained adapters are retained by the author. All reported scores and the primary analysis can be reproduced from the deposited responses without model weights. AI assistance and the prospective protocol amendment are disclosed.

title: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
abstract: From Quantum Beats to Topological Protection: A Stratum-Based Hybrid Architecture Integrating NV Centers, Weyl Interfaces, and Majorana Qubits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Mehmet Keçeci Orcid: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9937-9839 Abstract: The realization of scalable and fault-tolerant quantum computing systems requires not only the development of qubits with long coherence times but also the integration of heterogeneous physical platforms within a unified architectural framework. This study proposes a Stratum-based hybrid quantum computing architecture that combines the precise quantum state control enabled by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, the topological interface properties of Weyl semimetals, and the intrinsic error resilience provided by Majorana zero modes. The primary objective of this work is to establish a theoretical foundation for next-generation fault-tolerant quantum systems by integrating high-fidelity spin manipulation mechanisms derived from quantum beat phenomena with topologically protected information-processing layers. Within the proposed framework, the Stratum Model conceptualizes each physical, functional, and topological component of the quantum architecture as an independent yet dynamically interacting layer. NV centers constitute the control and sensing strata responsible for quantum state preparation, precision measurements, quantum memory operations, and quantum network node functionalities. Quantum beats serve as a dynamic characterization mechanism for spin superposition states within these layers, enabling high-accuracy monitoring and manipulation of coherent quantum dynamics. In contrast, Weyl interfaces are modeled as intermediary topological strata that govern transitions between distinct topological phases while facilitating robust and protected transfer of quantum information carriers across heterogeneous subsystems. At the highest operational level, Majorana qubits form the topological computing layer of the architecture. Through nonlocal quantum information encoding, they provide inherent robustness against environmental noise, decoherence, and local perturbations. Interactions among architectural layers are defined not only by physical interconnections but also through topological invariants, connectivity structures, error-propagation pathways, and quantum information flow dynamics. In this context, the Stratum approach extends beyond conventional spatial-layer descriptions by incorporating layer diversity, topological protection mechanisms, qubit heterogeneity, and fabrication imperfections into a common analytical framework. Furthermore, the model introduces novel design strategies for isolating defective or degraded strata, preserving critical topological regions, and mitigating system-level error propagation. The findings suggest that the integration of the precise quantum control capabilities of NV centers with the intrinsic topological protection offered by Majorana-based platforms may generate a powerful synergistic effect capable of enhancing quantum computational performance. Weyl interfaces are proposed to act as both physical and topological bridges between these two paradigms, enabling coherent communication across distinct quantum subsystems. Consequently, the proposed Stratum-based hybrid architecture provides an integrated design paradigm applicable to a broad spectrum of emerging quantum technologies, ranging from quantum sensing and distributed quantum networks to topological quantum processors and large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. title: BanglaBBQ: A Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Bangladeshi Context
abstract: This paper introduces BanglaBBQ, a question-answering bias benchmark designed to capture stereotypes grounded in the Bangladeshi context, in both Bangla and English. Following KoBBQ and PakBBQ, BanglaBBQ adapts the original Bias Benchmark for Question Answering (BBQ) by classifying its templates into three groups: directly translated (DT), modified to align target groups or contexts with Bangladesh (TM), and removed when deemed unsuitable for the Bangladeshi context (SR). This process retains 140 templates across six categories, comprising 76 DT and 64 TM templates. Five newly authored (NA) categories, based on stereotypes common in Bangladeshi society, are then added: marital status, age and political perception, regional origin, educational background, and mental-health status. Native Bangladeshi annotators judged all 466 newly authored templates, and 372 were retained because a strict majority of English annotators identified the intended target and rated the attitude as common enough. Each newly authored template is linked to a documented source and a verbatim quote from it. Each evaluated template also has a counter-stereotypical version of its disambiguated context. The dataset was evaluated using two open-weight models (Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B) and two closed models (GPT-4.1-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash). All four lean towards the stereotyped person when the context is ambiguous, in both languages, and the effect of language differs by model, so English results do not predict behaviour in Bangla. On the adapted BBQ templates, both Qwen3 models are also less accurate when the context contradicts a stereotype than when it confirms it. On the newly authored templates, the closed models follow counter-stereotypical evidence almost perfectly, and all four models are more biased on the templates that annotators validated than on those they rejected.

title: Code and synthetic data for certified entropic reconciliation of overlapping probabilistic models for decision making
abstract: This record contains the code and synthetic data supporting the computational results in “Certified entropic reconciliation of overlapping probabilistic models for decision making.” The ZIP archive includes five Python scripts, five JSON files with complete case records, and a README with reproduction instructions. The materials cover the 72-case comparison, a 144-case weight extension, rational optimization and decision certificates, casewise expected-loss transfer to two unrounded source specifications, a 15-clique decision example, and timing measurements. The rational-input certificates cover both expected loss and CVaR; the unrounded-source transfer is certified for expected loss only. The reference environment was Python 3.12.14 with NumPy 2.3.5. All inputs are synthetic; the archive contains no personal or confidential data.

title: ChainFL-RA: Blockchain-Enabled Decentralized Federated Learning with Reputation-Weighted Robust Aggregation and On-Chain Auditable Incentives
abstract: Official implementation and experimental artifacts of ChainFL-RA, a blockchain-enabled decentralized federated learning framework that unifies robust aggregation, on-chain reputation, and token settlement under a single verifiable quality signal. The same per-update evidence — cosine similarity to a momentum-anchored robust reference, guarded by a magnitude check — simultaneously determines (1) aggregation weights (reputation-weighted robust aggregation, RAgg), (2) on-chain reputation (slash-only memory with slow recovery), and (3) token settlement (smart-contract rewards and penalties). Every decision is committed to a hash-chained, validator-re-executable ledger. RAgg requires neither a clean validation set nor knowledge of the number of adversaries. Evaluated against FedAvg, Krum, FedRoLA, and FLAME on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 under label-flipping, update-scaling, and an adaptive Min-Max attack at 10–30% malicious ratios, ChainFL-RA is the only method that remains robust in every setting. The repository contains the full source code, 693-job experiment pipeline, raw per-round CSV outputs, analysis scripts, and all paper figures.

title: Paired-Outcome Learning for Selective Spacecraft Attitude Capture under Torque Limits
abstract: Torque-limited spacecraft attitude capture requires adapting the maneuver speed to uncertain braking authority. Faster settings can reduce average tracking error while worsening individual maneuvers, making selective modification of an existing controller a baseline-relative learning problem. A paired-outcome method combines three mechanisms: physically interpretable continuation policies with different speed envelopes, separate prediction of task failure and successful-pair tracking gains, and context-dependent rejection that executes the unchanged baseline. Complete paired simulations provide labels under common plant parameters and measurement seeds; training, validation, and calibration are separated by context. Basilisk experiments use 108 development contexts, 324 labeling rollouts, and 624 evaluation episodes across 48 test contexts, including disclosed post-freeze diagnostics. The selective controller reduces aggregate integrated attitude error by 4.67% relative to the branch baseline, with 17 improvements, 31 exact ties, and no observed regressions. Always using the fast alternative achieves a 4.81% reduction but worsens 11 cases. Gains occur in principal-axis, near-axis, braking-boundary, and selected noise/drift maneuvers; general coupled cases retain the baseline. Ablations show no additional aggregate benefit from branch commitment, active querying, or score subtraction. The evidence supports a restricted empirical trade-off between average improvement and individual regression, without establishing a closed-loop safety guarantee.

title: When Graph Autoencoders Look the Wrong Way: Complexity Bias and Simple Baselines in Unsupervised Anomaly Detection on the LHC Olympics 2020 Dataset (preprint and code)
abstract: Preprint and full code. Graph autoencoders trained on background-only events of the LHC Olympics 2020 R&D dataset give inverted anomaly scores (AUC 0.40-0.44), while the label-free mean transverse momentum per particle (HT/N) reaches AUC 0.811. Correlation and within-bin analyses link the inversion of the latent-density scores to event complexity. The paper is in paper/main.pdf. Trained checkpoints and per-event test scores: https://huggingface.co/Viverun/lhco-rnd-event-gae.

This record fixes, before data collection, the frozen protocol, the stimulus generator and evaluation data (r1), and the LLM harness and analysis code (h1.3) for the WGF v0.1 pilot. Study: whether presenting world state and usage rules as separated records (condition C) improves the joint accuracy of six derived cells on an artificial-verb task (T3), compared with B′, which presents the same records in the same order under a single integrated heading. title: Towards the Validation of Formal Explainers
abstract: Abstract Formal explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) offers unique theoretical guarantees of rigor when compared to other non-formal methods of explainability. However, little attention has been given to the validating practical implementations of formal explainers. This paper develops a novel methodology for validating formal explainers and reports on the assessment of the publicly available formal explainer PyXAI. The paper documents the existence of incorrect explanations computed by PyXAI on most of the datasets analyzed in the experiments, thereby confirming the importance of the proposed novel methodology for the validation of formal explainers.

title: An Adaptive Explainable AI Framework for Reliable Decision-making in Real-world Environments
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly support decisions in environments where data distributions, operational conditions, user needs, and risk levels change over time. Models that perform well during development may become unreliable after deployment because of data drift, concept drift, sensor degradation, population changes, or unexpected interactions. At the same time, predictive performance alone is insufficient for high-impact decisions: users need explanations that are understandable, relevant to the decision context, and accompanied by appropriate uncertainty information. This paper proposes an Adaptive Explainable AI (A-XAI) framework intended to integrate reliability monitoring, explanation generation, uncertainty estimation, human oversight, and controlled model adaptation within a unified lifecycle. The framework contains nine conceptual components: contextual data acquisition; data-quality, privacy, and drift assessment; prediction with uncertainty estimation; context-sensitive explanation generation; decision support and human oversight; risk-aware reliability gating; feedback and audit logging; controlled adaptation; and post-adaptation revalidation with version control. A formal decision policy is presented to connect predictive confidence, drift evidence, explanation quality, and consequence severity to actions such as automated recommendation, human review, abstention, or retraining. The paper also proposes an evaluation protocol spanning predictive performance, calibration, robustness, explanation fidelity and stability, fairness, latency, and operational outcomes. As a conceptual contribution, the framework is not presented as experimentally validated; its effectiveness must be tested in domain-specific studies using real deployment data and preregistered evaluation criteria. The proposed design offers a structured basis for developing AI systems that remain interpretable and risk-aware as real-world conditions evolve.

title: Evie's Pure Form RSI: Exact Readout Guarantees for Photonic Self-Modification under Transfer Uncertainty and Shared Noise
abstract: A readout sufficient for a system’s current task can become insufficient when its transfer function changes or a later module shares its noise. This research develops exact and approximate statistical guarantees for readout transformations in recursively reconfigured photonic systems. The central object is an implementable reconstruction kernel that preserves a declared statistical experiment across an entire class of possible modifications. The framework connects photonic readout design with Blackwell comparison, directed Le Cam deficiency, Gaussian experiment reconstruction, and finite-channel verification. PureOne/Evies-Pure-Form-RSI · Datasets at Hugging Face Uniform preservation under transfer uncertainty and future coupling Consider a linear Gaussian observation Y = Hθ + ε, where the realized transfer matrix H is unknown within a declared class. Let S span every possible signal direction in that class. Future observations may couple to the same noise through directions contained in a declared subspace E. For fixed equal-noise acquisition, a common parameter neighborhood of zero, and the stated Gaussian assumptions, the manuscript proves that one reconstruction kernel, independent of the realized transfer and future extension, preserves the complete joint experiment exactly if and only if the retained readout space contains S + E. Consequently, the minimum number of retained current linear real-mode coordinates is: r_min = dim(S + E). The result identifies why current-task compression can fail after reconfiguration: a discarded coordinate may later become a valuable noise reference. An exact KL-divergence identity quantifies approximate reconstruction by separating omitted signal from lost shared-noise correlations. Unknown-transfer reconstruction and controlled approximation For unequal Gaussian readout variances, the release derives the necessary-and-sufficient common-kernel criterion: γ UᵀQQᵀU ⪰ I, where U spans the full mutation space, Q defines the retained projection, and γ is the variance-ratio gain. Necessity follows from score identities joined across transfer models at their common null distribution; sufficiency follows from an explicit Gaussian reconstruction channel. An illustrative 32-mode rotation family requires all 32 coordinates for the stated exact uniform guarantee on every nonzero drift interval. Three derivative-Krylov coordinates instead provide a rigorous uniform total-variation reconstruction allowance of 0.0010638458. A declared resource ledger charging bounded signal-photon use permits 2.3 times exposure at equal budget. These are analytical and numerical model results. Exact comparison of visible verifier catalogues For finite fully permutation-equivariant source experiments, the manuscript reduces directed deficiency to visible nonnegative reliability catalogues to a scalar stop-loss comparison of normalized posterior MAP confidence. The result includes an attaining stochastic compiler, finite threshold witnesses, and counterexamples delimiting the scope of confidence-based comparison. An explicit separation between exact encoding and approximate simulation An affine-bilinear construction has uninformative singleton outputs, exact sufficient encoding dimension 3k, and exponentially vanishing joint information. A zero-readout simulator approximates the complete experiment with worst-state deficiency at most 2⁻ᵏ. The encoding lower bound applies to one realized observation under the specified query model; hidden-source flags or a separate seed-channel oracle change that acquisition problem. Reproducibility and evidence The release includes a 46-page manuscript, proofs, counterexamples, 14 executable scientific modules, detailed numerical reports, figures, provenance, and 1,247 normalized unrestricted-channel LP comparisons. Additional checks cover joint Gaussian reconstruction, strict deletion witnesses, the KL identity, and exact finite-field reconstruction. All declared software checks pass. The work provides mathematical acceptance conditions for bounded changes to evidence acquisition. Its guarantees require the stated transfer, covariance, interface, and calibration assumptions. Classical statistical comparison, weak transport, sufficient statistics, and Krylov methods are credited explicitly. Photonic hardware performance, general recursive intelligence gains, and independent priority remain unestablished.

title: tabray
abstract: tabray is a Python Package for generating tabular and array data structures with different topologies. It currently writes to netCDF for arrays and parquet for tabular, but I'd like to add Zarr in the near future. Besides generating data, the package can describe any netCDF or parquet dataset: dimensions, density and overlap of each variable. Describing a real dataset gives the parameters to generate a synthetic one like it

title: Weather route planning for ships based on improved grey wolf optimization
abstract: As the shipping industry transitions toward intelligence, weather route planning is essential for energy efficiency, operational performance, and safety. The Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is widely used in path planning, but its application to weather routing suffers from inadequate balance between global and local search and premature convergence. To improve search accuracy and adaptability for ship routing optimization, this paper proposed an improved GWO that integrates golden sine search and dimension learning-based hunting strategy (GSDLHGWO). The golden sine mechanism enhanced population diversity and provided macroscopic directional guidance, while an adaptive neighborhood learning scheme performed microscopic dimension-wise corrections to balance exploration and exploitation. The improved algorithm was embedded into the Pareto multi-objective framework to obtain trade-off solutions among multiple objectives. The statistical results of single-objective experiments across multiple scenarios demonstrated that GSDLHGWO achieved substantial and statistically significant fuel savings across most scenarios while remaining competitive in voyage time minimization. In multi-objective tests, the algorithm yielded wider-coverage Pareto fronts with better diversity, producing multiple balanced and feasible routes. Overall, the proposed algorithm exhibits superior optimization capability, providing effective technical support for safe and efficient route planning in smart shipping.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven reconfiguration of customer experience: A service-dominant logic framework
abstract: This study develops a framework explaining how artificial intelligence (AI) reconfigures customer experience in hospitality and tourism, drawing on service-dominant logic. Co-citation and content analyses were conducted to synthesize 89 articles and identify the intellectual structure of the literature. The findings reveal that institutional arrangements condition AI's legitimate participation in service ecosystems. Three mechanisms explain how AI reconfigures customer experience: the actor role architect, the interaction mediator, and the experience orchestrator. These mechanisms operate concurrently and recursively rather than as discrete stages within AI-enabled service ecosystems. The study makes three contributions to the literature. First, it positions customer experience reconfiguration as an ecosystem-level process. Second, it extends service-dominant logic from dyadic to triadic human-AI-human value co-creation. Third, it differentiates AI by functional intelligence, showing that mechanical, thinking, feeling, and multi-functional types perform distinct roles in this reconfiguration.
